# Repeated serial benchmark protocol

The proof runner records independent JVM launches, uses interleaved condition
ordering and retains failures. The coordinator exclusively owns the GPU and must
close preview clients first. This tooling does not establish any new performance
result by itself.

## Inputs and controls

Prepare isolated profiles using the coordinator's proof-profile preparation
script under `run-workloads/photon-proof/`. Each scene contains `high`,
`patched-off`, and `adaptive` profiles. Original `high` has no ShaderLOD mod;
`patched-off` loads the patched pack and mod with its live config disabled;
`adaptive` enables distance logic. Include the simpler `lower` quality control
where appropriate. Shared `control.json` must not override `enabled` or terrain
settings when testing shader-only benefits. All profiles must derive from the
same warmed source save and carry `workload-manifest.json` provenance.

Iris requires Sodium on this target. `minimal` therefore means Iris/Sodium plus
required runtime components, without additional optional optimizers. `optimized`
adds the coordinator's pinned optional mod stack. The runner passes
`-PperformanceStack=minimal/optimized` and `-PincludeDh=true/false` to Gradle.
Actual loaded mod IDs/versions and profile mod-jar SHA-256 hashes are captured;
request labels alone are not evidence that a stack loaded successfully.

Before the first launch, the runner hashes archives, shader options, camera
control, scene provenance, and relevant config files. It verifies stable shader,
camera and source identity again before each repeat. Minecraft legitimately
rewrites `options.txt` at shutdown, so its hash is recorded but not treated as an
immutable subsequent-launch input. Iris also rewrites pack option files with a
timestamp and removes explicit default values. Raw option-file bytes are retained
as evidence but are **not** compared with prelaunch bytes. The runner parses pack
source defaults to normalize requested input files, then validates every requested
active option against Iris's loaded effective values. Unrecognized requests fail;
only an unchanged upstream `INFO` default can be absent, because that profile
information selector is not asserted to control performance.

The runtime reads `Iris.getCurrentPack().get().getShaderPackOptions()`, enumerates
`getOptionSet().getBooleanOptions()/getStringOptions()`, and resolves values with
`getOptionValues().getBooleanValueOrDefault(name)/getStringValueOrDefault(name)`.
It records the sorted complete effective map and canonical JSON SHA-256 at both
measurement boundaries. These APIs were inspected in the pinned Iris jar.
Effective values must stay identical throughout capture and across repeat
launches for the same condition. Paired quality comparison uses these loaded
values, including defaults, instead of incomplete normalized option-file text.
Actual framebuffer, requested/effective
radius, camera, day/weather, enabled/preset state and Iris pipeline state are
captured at both measurement boundaries. Changed inputs, disabled shaders,
fallback, wrong pack or wrong LOD state invalidate the run. Source-save hashes
are preparation provenance; they do not assert byte-for-byte equality of mutable
save files after Minecraft has written them.

A per-run UUID in `workload-request.json` must match the fresh report. Prior
reports move into the output directory; an old report cannot satisfy a new run.
The runner checks process exclusion, waits for the complete Gradle/JVM exit,
rejects fatal shader/control/write error markers, and preserves invalid fresh
reports. On timeout it terminates only its own process group. Known resource
property and audio warnings are not automatically treated as shader failures.
There is also an advisory lock preventing two matrix runners at once. Process
inspection covers the project's dev launchers and common direct Minecraft Java
launchers; manually operated exotic launchers still require operator exclusion.

Each condition appears once in each repeat block. Williams rows balance order
positions and carryover over a complete design cycle; a partial 3–5-repeat cycle
is interleaved but is **not** claimed perfectly balanced. A two-condition,
four-repeat matrix gives AB/BA/AB/BA. Both runtime stacks can be interleaved in
one matrix instead of measuring the whole minimal stack before optimized.

## Commands

Start with a dry run (no writes, build or client launch):

```sh
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py forest-high forest-patched-off forest-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal optimized --repeats 3 --dry-run
```

Suggested initial matrices, once every profile and optional stack has passed a
runtime smoke check:

```sh
# Ordinary scene, ShaderLOD incremental gain within each stack: 18 JVM runs.
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py forest-high forest-patched-off forest-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal optimized --repeats 3 --tag forest-stacks-r3
# Premium cloud scene plus simpler existing-quality control: 12 JVM runs.
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py cloud-high cloud-patched-off cloud-adaptive cloud-lower --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal --repeats 3 --tag cloud-controls-r3
# DH-absent compatibility/performance path: 9 JVM runs.
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py forest-high forest-patched-off forest-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal --dh absent --repeats 3 --tag forest-no-dh-r3
# Refine a promising ordinary-scene result with five additional independent pairs.
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py forest-high forest-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal --repeats 5 --tag forest-confirm-r5
```

Default warmup is 45 seconds, capture 30 seconds, timeout 300 seconds. Add JVM
startup/shutdown time: 18 runs take at least 22.5 minutes of warmup/capture and
usually substantially longer. Prefer completing one matrix before expanding the
set. `--skip-build` skips only the initial build. `--warmup`, `--duration`,
`--timeout`, `--sample-interval`, and `--no-gpu-queries` are explicit controls;
keep them matched within a comparison. CPU wall/thread clocks remain separate
from actual GPU measurements. CPU layer profiling is disabled by default in the
runner to reduce measurement overhead.

## Analysis and uncertainty

Each new tag produces `dev/logs/TAG/matrix-manifest.json`, console logs,
measurements, summaries and `matrix-analysis.json`. Existing tags are refused.
Failed matrices remain marked failed and are not silently ranked. Rerun with a
new tag after correcting the failure; preserve the failed evidence.
The initial `sustained-v2-main` matrix is retained as failed: its first baseline
hit the old raw-file guard after Iris normalized an otherwise equivalent option
file. This was a tooling mismatch, not a demonstrated shader-quality change.

The analysis reports the median, min/max and median absolute deviation across
**independent JVM runs** for FPS-derived frame duration, GPU mean/median/p95,
CPU wall/thread means and CPU wall p95. Candidate time reductions are paired
against the scene's original-high run in the same repeat block and runtime
stack. Positive percentages mean lower time. Runtime-stack comparisons are
separate from ShaderLOD's incremental comparisons. Geometry/detail changes and
simpler quality controls are annotated; upstream quality settings must match for
adaptive and patched-disabled comparisons.

Frame samples are autocorrelated. Thousands of frames are not thousands of
independent replicates. No IID confidence interval or significance claim is
produced. Three to five repeats remain exploratory; per-run p95 describes tail
latency and is not uncertainty on the speedup. Order drift, shared hardware
activity and thermal/cache state can still matter. Do not choose the best repeat
or drop an anomalous run because it weakens the result.

GPU scope boundaries, coarse Apple elapsed-query attribution, CPU/driver time
and overlapping scopes retain the limits in [GPU_TIMING.md](GPU_TIMING.md).
Correct timings do not prove visual quality: inspect transitions, motion and
salient lighting separately.

## Wetness and temporal observation

The dev harness now wraps the existing wetness `FloatSupplier` at the exact
pinned Iris 1.8.12 `CommonUniforms.generalCommonUniforms` registration. The
`UniformHolder.uniform1f` call is sliced between the `wetness` and `skyColor`
string constants and requires one match. The actual registration uses
`PER_TICK`. There is no `WorldInfoUniforms` class in this artifact. The original
supplier is evaluated exactly once each time Iris normally evaluates it; the
tracker never invokes a smoother while exporting a snapshot or reading back GL.

Separate registrations can own separate smoothers. Telemetry therefore retains
bounded registration IDs, holder class/frequency labels, per-supplier raw/applied
last values, ranges and read counts. Those IDs are not shader program IDs:
program identity is explicitly unknown. An overall latest value cannot prove
all programs share the same state. The tracker makes no per-evaluation
allocations; registration and snapshot allocations happen outside frame hot
hooks. Capacity exhaustion fails visibly instead of silently omitting suppliers.

`shader_temporal_inputs_initial/start/end` are exported separately from the
strict input-state comparison. They include actual observed wetness and CPU
source getters for frame counter, frame time, frameTimeCounter, full day time,
world day/time, moon phase, rainStrength and Photon's derived world-age formula.
The source getters are not a readback of uploaded custom uniforms; biome
smoothing and all GPU histories remain unobserved. FrameCounter and real clocks
continue advancing. Normal dynamic wetness changes are labeled in the matrix
run metadata and do not invalidate exploratory captures merely because the
smoother advances. Missing observations are labeled explicitly.

An optional artificial steady shader-weather control is available:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py cloud-high cloud-patched-off cloud-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof-v2 --stacks minimal --repeats 3 --warmup 35 --duration 20 --fixed-wetness 1 --tag cloud-fixed-wetness-r3
```

`--fixed-wetness` accepts finite values from 0 to 1 and maps to
`-PfixedWetness` / `shaderlod.dev.fixedWetness`. It applies from initial uniform
registration throughout warmup/capture, not by jumping weather at measurement
start. Every wrapped supplier still evaluates its original raw smoother once,
then publishes the fixed diagnostic value. Real rainStrength, smoothing clocks,
frameCounter and animation clocks remain unchanged. Per-registration observations
must prove the requested applied value at both boundaries and throughout the
capture range. Missing or wrong fixed telemetry fails the run. A default run
preserves the original wetness value exactly and rejects an unexpected fixed
policy. This is dev-only instrumentation and never a production weather feature.

The original 36-run matrix predates this telemetry and must not be retrospectively
claimed to have matched actual shader wetness. See
[PHOTON_TEMPORAL_INPUTS.md](PHOTON_TEMPORAL_INPUTS.md) for the source-based
hypothesis and remaining unmeasured state.

## Per-repeat images

After the complete client JVM closes, the runner preserves that repeat's fresh
`screenshots/workload-final.png` as `NNN-bB-CASE-STACK-final.png` in the matrix
output, with path and SHA-256 in its row. It checks freshness and PNG signature;
stale/missing images fail the run. Copying/hashing occurs after timing. The report
and image are retained before subsequent profile captures overwrite them.
Earlier matrix runs did not preserve every repeated image this way; no missing
image is fabricated retroactively.

Implementation checks passed: standalone Java policy/supplier tests verify
clamping, property bounds, original evaluation once, distinct raw suppliers,
fixed publishing and snapshot read independence; Python tests check all observed
supplier guards, dynamic drift, missing/stale image handling and PNG preservation.
`compileDevClientJava` passed. These checks do not establish runtime mixin
application. Before the next measured matrix, verify a real original/mod-absent
capture has supplier observations, fixed 1 reaches every observed registration,
raw values continue evolving, clocks/counters advance, and a fresh image is
preserved. Then run matched dynamic/fixed repeated controls and inspect images.

The prepared-camera guard compares yaw modulo 360 because Minecraft wraps yaw:
180, -180 and 540 degrees represent the same heading. XYZ and pitch comparisons
remain linear with the same 0.002 tolerance. Both prepared and observed camera
values must be finite numeric values; missing values, booleans, strings, NaN and
infinity are rejected before modular arithmetic. The failed
`ssr-original-probe` remains excluded from accepted performance evidence: its
180/-180 guard mismatch was corrected in tooling, not retrospectively accepted.

# Fresh-client Fabric BSL native baseline diagnostic

Two independently launched native-only Off clients completed the prepared single-window consumer on October 11, 2026. Original measured **24.5787 ms/frame** and fresh original-return **20.0677 ms/frame**, a **−18.3532%** native frame-cost change. Both passed every measured-frame pacing/focus/viewport/core admission. This still leaves substantial native-only variability; it establishes neither an optimization gain nor the cause of historical lifetime drift. The fixed Fabric BSL optimization trial remains closed.

| Observation | Fresh original | Fresh original-return |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed world-render frames | 1,221 | 1,497 |
| Elapsed window seconds | 30.01057 | 30.04134 |
| Measured-start client age, seconds | 66.0349 | 61.5466 |
| Stable-world-start client age, seconds | 25.9949 | 21.5311 |
| Launcher-to-ready seconds | 33.27 | 28.04 |
| Captured UTC | 08:47:55.045484 | 08:50:07.587923 |
| Invalid measured frames | 0 | 0 |

Age derives from the saved snapshot time minus elapsed/stable seconds against recorded process birth (one-second precision). Warmup differs by approximately 4.49 seconds; these are nearby early-client ages, not exactly matched ages. No rebase, restart or scene/preset/filter adjustment was used. The prior same-client native control measured 10.85 → 13.01 → 30.98 ms/frame; its historical evidence is preserved rather than pooled with this protocol.

Apple M3 Max (30 GPU cores, 36 GB), macOS 27.0, OpenGL 4.1 Metal 91.7, Java 21; Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric 0.19.5/API 0.116.17, Iris 1.8.8, Sodium 0.6.13. BSL 10.1.8 original SHA-256 `36b0a50ff7918bf10e9422c401d93779f9d0088a26acea975b435243f96930b5` loaded with its certified 384-option native map, empty overrides, core Off/Performance/debug false, fullscreen native 1920×1200, vsync false, configured/stored/effective cap 260 and render distance 24. DH absent. Both snapshots match camera (256.5,95,768.5), yaw135/pitch9, day7000, clear weather and selected resources. Fresh APFS world clones matched all 237 canonical files before launch; canonical remained unchanged after both runs.

Actually verified: handback source pins (only the already-adopted offline checker differed), produced OriginalSourceChecksMain and NativeCostChecksMain, single-phase bytecode/resource joins, fresh source/class/resource/main-jar freezes, both prepared and launch saved-plan preflights, driver-loaded shader/native viewport, all 2,718 measured-frame observations, unchanged loaded options/core/archive, zero helper/compactor/input/output/reduced-batch counters and no production Apply/reload. No new build was required. Each client used the existing `dev_client` supervisor with a fresh Fabric-specific frozen-consumer guard; exact commands, PID/birth/argv, focus and stop proofs are in each arm’s owner/launch/receipt files. Generated classpath/config were saved after return; original generated argument-file bytes were not captured independently.

Both stills were visually inspected: native landscape/foliage/water/clouds rendered without obvious corruption. Original has a movement tutorial toast, return does not; its measured-window duration was not observed. Exact pixel equivalence, motion quality, DH/PBR, changed-shader consumption/work reduction and production restoration are unverified. “Original-return” denotes the second independent native client, not an Off-after-On restoration test.

[Raw evidence](../../dev/logs/speed-port-r1/fresh-client-baseline-20261011/) includes `comparison.json`, `quality-observations.json`, `produced-class-checks.json`, per-arm `runtime-report.json`, `launch-plan.json`, `owner.json`, freezes and screenshots. Exact owned clients PID81326 and PID81791 were stopped with `dev_client.py stop --session`; absence and lock release were verified, preserving the historical Gradle daemon. [Final release](../../dev/logs/speed-port-r1/fresh-client-baseline-20261011/final-release.json) observed 08:51:04 UTC; lane transferred to parent, no owned live processes. All setup/repairs/checks/execution/reporting finished within the acknowledged 15-minute review budget. Parent should accept this bounded diagnostic as native variability evidence and select a distinct runnable source/driver route; this result does not complete the cross-version/loader project.

records.text:
# ShaderLOD project overview

ShaderLOD explores reducing expensive Photon shader work as scene distance
increases. The first platform is NeoForge with Iris required. Photon is the
explicit compatibility target, and DH is optional for the mod while included
in the development runtime for compatibility checks.

The initial distance proposal is full quality through 32 blocks, medium quality
through 96 blocks, and low quality beyond that. These are starting defaults,
not a measured optimum. Define distance in camera-relative block units and
use transition bands or stable dithering to avoid a visible moving ring.

## Development sequence

1. Establish a reproducible NeoForge client skeleton and compatible Iris,
   Sodium, Photon, and DH runtime. Add durable goal/team infrastructure and a
   small LOD foundation that can be inspected and tested.
2. Prove one distance-sensitive Photon effect works under Iris with DH absent.
   Compare the same scene with the change disabled and enabled; inspect both
   visual transitions and GPU execution time before expanding infrastructure.
3. Build the Photon MVP around several measured effects. Candidate effects are
   POM/material work, shadow filtering, and SSR. Add validated configuration
   transport and useful quality presets as evidence supports them.
4. Extend LOD to DH terrain/water/shadows and validate the vanilla/DH boundary.
   Keep DH optional and test both installed and absent configurations.

## Architecture boundaries

The NeoForge client mod owns config, loader/runtime detection, and integration
lifecycle. Photon owns explicit GLSL LOD logic through a pinned, maintained
patch or derivative. Iris provides the shader runtime. DH extends terrain
rendering and eventually needs dedicated integration checks.

A Java config file does not automatically become an Iris custom uniform.
Document and test the actual bridge before claiming the mod controls shader
quality live. Shader-pack options can support the first proof independently.
Do not expand into automatic rewriting of arbitrary shader packs during setup.

## Initial risks

Distance branches may save little GPU work when neighboring pixels diverge.
Some effects cannot safely change samples or ray-march steps without changing
appearance or temporal stability. Loader and renderer versions must be
compatible as a set. Photon may require hardware/driver features unavailable
on the development Mac; record this as a runtime limit rather than calling
static source inspection a rendering pass.

The setup goal establishes an environment and evidence base. It does not
promise an FPS gain, freeze the product's final quality thresholds, or complete
the later Photon/DH MVP.

# General shared LOD performance pilot

2026-10-05 protocol, written before timing. This operation measures the current
general shared-volume system in000f355, with Photon as its first explicit reference
consumer. It introduces no pack tuning, shader knobs or quality reduction. This
is a qualified pilot; it cannot establish the50% goal, physical integration counts,
near/far parity, still/motion quality, DH or another hardware target.

## Acceptance fixed before launch

Nine independent JVMs form three blocks: original/disabled/adaptive,
disabled/adaptive/original, adaptive/original/disabled. Each arm occurs once in
each position; this balances position, not full carryover. All nine profiles are
prepared before timing, from the same stopped canonical coastal save. Independent
copies avoid repeat-JVM save/config history. The original has upstream Photon and
no main mod. Disabled/adaptive use the same exact registered private source with
integration optionTRUE; only the global mod enable differs. Seven effect sections
retain the existing512/1536/128/.85/.75 ADAPTIVE request for volume, INHERIT/unity
for the others, and salient-lighting protection. No config/source/class update is
permitted during the batch; NeoForge's semantic-equivalent comment/layout rewrite
is retained and qualified.

Current JAR must be
`aa65cf9157e0c5dac7db6ea65d38a42b3eec06a71838e394389063ead5b3e672`;
the complete class/resource member inventories freeze at batch start. Original
source120897… and private5de756…/manifest40efd7…/complete metadata/helpers/license
remain strict. Actual366 upstream effective options must match the canonical map
exactly. Only the declared integration=true flag is added for the private arms;
no arbitrary private-option exemption or old combined family is used. Current
typed schema1/availability1 linkage is separately established by
`dev/logs/shared-lod-system-qa-r2/shared-lod-terminal-audit.json`.
Observers/readbacks remain off throughout timing, so that linkage is not asserted
as newly sampled for each timed program.

Every run must pass existing matrix UUID/input/mod/source/noFallback/pose and
optional-stack/temporal validators, plus exact shared-system gates:

- Native WINDOWED2976×1672, logical1488×836, visible/non-iconified and stable
  UNFOCUSED throughout every sampled capture observation, with zero transitions.
- Fixed coastal500.5/68/660.5, yaw87.38/pitch3.735, time12500, clear weather,
  observed fixed wetness0, native24 detailed chunks, minimal Iris/Sodium/noDH.
- Identical pacing: frame limit260, vsyncfalse, pause-on-lost-focusfalse. Each
  warmup-only watcher arms before launch, activates Codex only after the camera is
  applied, then exits before capture. No focus changes during capture.
- Warmup25s/capture20s. Frame-only asynchronous GPUelapsed N5; actual samples
  must be game-render/measurement epoch2 at frame IDs1 modulo5. Pass/layer timers,
  sampler readback, DH evidence, water survey, shadow observer, visibility lists
  and coherence oracle are explicitlyOFF. Do not sum pass timings.
- All nine actual scene/runtime inventories match, apart from the intentional
  main-mod presence. All source and compiled inventories stay frozen. Every
  raw failure and run artifact is retained; the first failure stops the batch.
  Observation/tool timeout never restarts a client or substitutes another run.

Report per-run GPUelapsed and total-frame `run-tick` wall median/p95, and
elapsed-time/rendered-frame mean. Aggregate the three independent JVM values
per arm with median/min/max/MAD and paired per-block time reductions. Throughput
ratio is original elapsed-per-frame / adaptive elapsed-per-frame;1.5× means
50% higher throughput and33.333% less time for the same work. Frames are
autocorrelated samples, not independent experimental replicates. GPUelapsed
includes command-starvation intervals and is not GPU busy time. Real temporal
shader clocks/phase and final images are not frame-aligned across JVMs.

A useful consistent pilot signal requires all three original→adaptive blocks to
improve both GPUmedian and total-frame median, median paired reductions of at
least5% for both, and improved elapsed-per-frame throughput in each block. This
is a decision to consider a separately scoped query-free corroboration, not a
relaxed50% gate or accepted quality claim. This operation stops at nine runs and
analysis; no extra run chases a positive result. Quiet query-free corroboration
is useful only if that fixed signal exists.

## Ownership, commands and context

Root transferred sole GPU/client to `shared_system_runtime`. Both
`spatial_transitions` and `spatial_pipeline` acknowledged they will pause all
tests/builds/parsers/encoders for the entire batch; only lightweight source edits
may continue. They resume only after formal GPU return. No child worker is used.
The runner snapshots load and the top15 CPU processes only before/after runs;
it does not stop unrelated apps. Host activity remains a qualification, and
configured pacing does not prove scheduler/thermal-state equivalence.

Owned new files are `scripts/run_shared_lod_benchmark.py`,
`tests/test_shared_lod_benchmark.py` and this report. The wrapper reuses existing
matrix launch/validation functions through the explicit mapping:
original→water-high/runClientLodOff, disabled→water-patched-off/runClientLodOn,
adaptive→water-adaptive/runClientLodOn. Existing matrix/preparer/harness sources
are unedited. All generated worlds, captures, logs and inventories stay ignored.

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_shared_lod_benchmark.py -v
python3 scripts/run_shared_lod_benchmark.py --prepare \
  --profiles-root run-workloads/shared-lod-benchmark-r1
python3 scripts/run_shared_lod_benchmark.py --run \
  --profiles-root run-workloads/shared-lod-benchmark-r1 \
  --output dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-r1
```

The runner uses the existing proof-matrix lock and exclusive-runtime check.
Every exact Gradle command/request UUID and runner PID is recorded before launch;
the warmup watcher records actual client Java PID before capture. The existing
`wait_command` timeout/KeyboardInterrupt stops its owned child process group.
Never kill by broad process name. Exact runner exec/PID and formal return will be
recorded below when launched/terminal. Preparation and wrapper checks remain
pending at this protocol checkpoint; no timed client has been launched.

## Terminal result: incomplete batch, strict rejection retained

Six wrapper fixtures passed before launch, logged in
`dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-source-tests.log`. A fixture's initial temporary
path comparison failed because macOS resolves `/var` to `/private/var`; its
assertion was corrected to compare resolved paths. The initial failure is retained
in `dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-source-tests-first-failure.log`.
Actual preparation and nine-profile preflight completed; all initial worlds
matched canonical89c962…, exact source/member/metadata/config guards passed,
and class/resource inventories matched the previously verified current revision.
Evidence is `dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-preparation.json` and
`run-workloads/shared-lod-benchmark-r1/shared-benchmark-preparation.json`.

Runner exec25403/PID46215 launched three JVMs, then stopped at the first rejection.
Original/disabled passed individually. Adaptive rendered and passed its source,
effective options, scene, window, temporal and timing gates, but failed the
cross-run strict raw loaded-artifact inventory. No remaining block/run launched,
no timeout/restart occurred and no qualified exception was silently introduced.
Raw failed status and every O/D/A report remain preserved; there is no accepted
comparison, run spread, consistent signal, query-free corroboration or50% proof.

| Arm, block1 | Request UUID | Actual Java PID | GPUmedian/p95, ms | Total-frame wall median/p95, ms | GPU samples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | 1a89a508-dd60-44cb-8a19-f6b9f1ca71fa | 46239 | 15.124 / 16.845 | 16.222 / 23.353 | 243 |
| Disabled | f5584edd-6b8d-4fa4-b4e1-93cf9d627968 | 46402 | 15.737 / 18.032 | 16.617 / 23.599 | 235 |
| Adaptive, rejected comparison | 81a3ff67-315d-4db2-a5f4-a4bf638e0cad | 46553 | 25.949 / 33.238 | 26.726 / 36.671 | 144 |

These are raw diagnostic values, including the rejected adaptive report. They
are one serial block; no paired/repeated effect estimate is accepted. Original
capture01:19:08.993608Z–01:19:29.044594Z, disabled01:20:12.998113Z–01:20:33.043498Z,
adaptive01:21:15.889635Z–01:21:35.950255Z on2026-10-06UTC. Each warmup watcher
activated before capture, then stopped; exact commands and guard outcomes are
in `dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-r1/shared-benchmark-manifest.json`. Each native
capture stayed visible/non-iconified/unfocused with no window transition, no
fallback and exact held366upstream options. Observer/pass/layer properties were
off; GPUelapsed N5 and CPU measurement epoch/scope gates passed. The current
main/dev/resources remained frozen at terminal; source was unmodified. Images
are retained, but no quality inspection or comparison is promoted here.

The failed runner exited1; all three client Java PIDs and runner were verified
absent, and exclusive-runtime check returned no clients. Sole GPU/client formally
returned to root before diagnosis. Both spatial workers were notified they may
resume heavy checks. No owned live process remains, and no additional timed run
or build follows this batch.

## Read-only mismatch diagnosis

The sole raw artifact difference was `fabric_api_base`0.4.42+d1308ded19:
original/disabled loaded
`1aa448a0eff484c7b9f5a6aedbc5050a8d17999f31949dfebb20a7b977f80a07`;
adaptive loaded
`620fa28434a74dfa9e94af33a3e3bf70a939e9a4b0fcae1fbc01ba2c24f32531`.
The nested loader path serializes as an empty string, so the actual reported
hash and direct nested byte inventory establish origin. Source inspection did
not assume equivalence from a version string.

The read-only diagnosis re-extracted
`META-INF/jarjar/fabric-api-base-0.4.42+d1308ded19.jar` from the actual pinned

| Actual parent path | Actual parent SHA256 | Nested child SHA256 / size |

| dev/runtime/iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar | 3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83 | 620fa284… / 34807bytes |
| dev/runtime/sodium-neoforge-0.6.13+mc1.21.1.jar | 7acd7af2ef75ec883a6872c17494ead65e38025151eb08a1d60e36d34377f403 | 1aa448a0… / 34806bytes |

All three captures report Minecraft1.21.1/NeoForge21.1.253 against the actual
`build/moddev/artifacts/neoforge-21.1.253.jar` SHA256
`a3f878f97a229b543a2c872c4a3c03b19ebd3efbd11af2caed9c258c08aebf55`, independently
matched to current disk bytes. Iris1.8.12-snapshot+mc1.21.1-local and
Sodium0.6.13+mc1.21.1 actual loaded parent identities also match these bytes.
Recorded GPU/driver is Apple M3 Max/OpenGL4.1 Metal91.7; no target-hardware claim.

Both children have the same38 ZIP names, no duplicates, and20 regular files.
All17 class files, `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` and `assets/fabric-api-base/icon.png` are
byte-identical. The only differing payload is `META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`,
whose exact one-line NeoForge dependency lower bound is `[21.1.169,)` in Iris
versus `[21.1.115,)` in Sodium. Replacing that exact bound makes descriptors
byte-identical. Current21.1.253 satisfies both. Recomputed sorted member payload
fingerprints are classes
`34704804f9e2834e3114d6029792a5353bd1a09ea9fa814883bb912ca9ace10a`, unchanged
resources `4afce8cc02b58dc62b4faa2e6a5c8e75ec2bc9c76e348dea42491b0175ea2385`, and
all files except descriptor
`f075c9f89451356a91e59ff0c5a534c8358f3f7885747ad6c79a490cb5aceffa`.

This reproduces the exact narrowly reviewed condition in
[CULLING_EMBEDDED_PROVENANCE.md](CULLING_EMBEDDED_PROVENANCE.md) and
`dev/runtime-artifact-equivalences.json`. A read-only check against that registry
also finds every other loaded identity equal, excluding intentional main-mod
presence. No runtime transformed class bytes or resolver determinism were
observed. No failed report/manifest is relabeled, no runner gate changes and no
accepted performance comparison follow from this diagnosis. Root decides any
independent qualification or future experiment.

## Host context and coarse CPU trend

Outside-window prelaunch load averages(1/5/15min) were1.96/2.08/2.22,
2.88/2.38/2.33 and2.98/2.58/2.41 for O/D/A. Snapshots show WindowServer20.6%,
25.0%,32.3%; ChatGPT11.5%,91.6%,8.2%; adaptive prelaunch also has Dock9.9%.
Runner preflight/postrun hashing appears in its cumulative CPU snapshots. These
are process snapshots outside windows, not continuous capture-window load or
evidence of equivalent thermal/clocks/scheduling. No unrelated app was stopped.
Workers acknowledged heavy-check pause; runtime enforcement is not inferred
from that acknowledgment.

Exact nested entry hashes, metadata diff, real loaded parent/runtime hashes,
all raw CPU streams, host snapshots and diagnosis provenance are retained in
`dev/logs/shared-lod-benchmark-r1/failed-batch-provenance-diagnosis.json`.
The sole read-only diagnosis command was

source prep remain in their ignored roots. Scoped source/report whitespace checks
pass. This bounded operation ends with incomplete evidence and formal GPU return.

## Independent one-block qualification and future source freeze

After accepting the strict failed batch, root explicitly authorized a separate
derived qualification using the existing exact API Base registry. The new

# Captured shadow-frustum query replay

`scripts/replay_frustum_coherence.py` is an offline tuning tool for the pinned
Java helper. It never launches Minecraft or edits production code. Its inputs
are one captured first same-frame/base-frustum query sequence and the exact
helper source from that capture. This is a diagnostic cost model, not an FPS
or whole-frame performance measurement.

## Trace and provenance

The tool reads `shadow_coherence_oracle.replayTrace` from a workload report,
or the trace object directly. The capture worker owns its source/schema and
actual runtime recording. Required fields match the agreed capture record:

- `kind=BASE`, exact pinned `frustumClass`, `frustumIdentity`, `renderFrame`,
  `prepareOrPlaneGeneration`, `planeCount`.
- `contextAvailable` and context `available/ownerAssociationVerified` must be
  explicit true. Context identity/count must match the trace.
- Context `helperSourceSha256` must equal the actual source read by the tool.
  `fma` is an explicit boolean; `rawPlaneBits` contains only the active four-
  coefficient rows. `rawDistanceLimitBits` is signed/raw int64, with its kind
  and optional hexadecimal field checked against the same bytes.
- Ordered query rows start at index zero and contain six signed/raw int32
  `rawBoundsBits` endpoints plus `original` and `actual` booleans.
- Counts, `sequenceEnded`, `sequenceBoundaryObserved`, `truncated`, `complete`, `originalUnavailable` and
  `revisitedAfterClose` are explicit. Unknown context, unavailable original
  results or a revisited closed scope are rejected.

The capture's `proofCacheStateCaptured=false` is explicit. This replay starts
with an empty helper and cannot reconstruct runtime proofs created before the
first observed callback. Cold replay hit ratios can therefore differ from the
runtime counter distribution. An observed sequence boundary is required before
labeling a nontruncated capture complete; ending a measurement alone is weaker.

Float values are reconstructed in Java with `Float.intBitsToFloat`, and the
distance with `Double.longBitsToDouble`, via an explicit binary transfer.
Negative coordinates, signed zero and NaN payload bits are never recovered
from lossy decimal JSON. Non-finite inputs are retained and counted explicitly;
they are not silently excluded. A truncated/incomplete capture is marked as
**partial recorded prefix only**, never full-frame/world coverage.

Reversed captures are rejected by this initial tool. Their alternate distance
box acceptance requires additional context and its original ordering. Identity
hashes alone do not establish owner association; the capture must verify it.

## Explicit source variants

The actual `ShadowFrustumCoherence.java` and its actual pure-JDK
`ShadowFrustumCoherenceDiagnostics.java` are copied into generated directories.
Four exact single-occurrence source anchors may change:

1. Slot count: 64, 256 or 512.
2. Coarse lower-grid multiplier: 64, 32 or 16 blocks.
3. Coarse extent: grid +32 blocks, respectively 96/64/48.
4. Cell divisor: the same grid value.

The nine combinations are a fixed matrix, not a generic source rewriting
system. Every other helper expression/guard, including original floating-point
containment proof, remains identical. Missing/duplicated anchors fail. Each
variant gets its own source SHA, exact anchor change list and isolated compiler
output. Capture, original helper, diagnostics and Java runner hashes are recorded.

Prepare sources without Java execution:

```sh
python3 scripts/replay_frustum_coherence.py dev/logs/TRACE_REPORT.json \
  --output dev/logs/frustum-replay/unique-run
```

Only after the coordinator releases a CPU window, use a **new output path**:

```sh
python3 scripts/replay_frustum_coherence.py dev/logs/TRACE_REPORT.json \
  --output dev/logs/frustum-replay/unique-executed-run --execute
```

Generated artifacts must live under ignored `build/` or `dev/logs/`; existing
directories are refused. Java 21 is required and its version recorded. On Mac,
the tool resolves the installed Java 21 JDK; `--java-home` allows an explicit
path. Root continues to own runtime/GPU profiling and production integration.

## Correctness and counters

Each variant replays the same query order with a fresh helper context. The Java
runner independently reconstructs pinned Iris's full positive/negative
classifier and rejecting distance predicate, comparing that reference against
every captured original boolean. It also compares every candidate decision
`canAccept || fullOriginalFallback` to the same original. Any mismatch, including
captured actual-versus-original mismatch, makes execution fail.

The counter JVM enables the helper's original final diagnostic gate. It counts
selected fast accepts, new-proof versus cached-proof accepts, cached fallback,
new fallback, invalid AABBs and coarse containment fallback. A new proof accept
is not a reused proof. Reference rejects are separated into distance and plane
rejects; they do not prove that all such queries admit a shared outside proof.

`manifest.json` retains per-variant counts, generated sources, compiler logs
and raw replay stdout/stderr. Passing this bounded prefix does not establish
other frames, camera angles, daylight, dimensions or optional-mod compatibility.

## Optional diagnostic CPU timings

`--execute --timing` adds a separate JVM per variant with the final counter gate
false. Correctness is checked before warming/timing; mismatched variants are
not timed. Warmup/repeats are bounded and baseline/candidate measurement order
alternates. The timed candidate includes a new frame-local helper/arrays,
coarse checks and **full original fallback**, including child distance rejection
and both original plane expressions. Results consume a checksum. No timing
arm uses enabled diagnostic counters.

The model still omits actual Mixin/virtual call layout, frustum construction,
controller/accessor overhead, the visibility graph, driver submission and GPU
work. JIT inlining/escape analysis, GC and this one query distribution can differ
from Minecraft. A nanosecond ranking only selects candidates for real profiling;
it is not a frame gain or an operation-count guarantee. Any final implementation
needs matched original/disabled/enabled actual-frame runs and visual/caster checks.

## Later outside-proof hypothesis

The earlier aggregate oracle rejected about 31% of child queries. The new
replay reports actual captured reference distance/plane rejection counts, but
does not add rejection caching or change the production boolean API.

A future tri-state cache could prove **all contained children outside** when
the coarse box is strictly disjoint from a rejecting distance box, or when
the original positive-expression maximum vertex is strictly `< -plane.w`,
with finite coefficient/extreme evaluation guards. Weak monotonicity then
bounds every child's positive vertex below that same threshold. Tangency
cannot become a rejection. A remembered failed acceptance proof is not an
outside proof: overlapping/partial coarse boxes must retain original fallback.

For reversed frusta, a plane-outside proof is insufficient when any child can
hit the alternate box's early acceptance. Require the entire coarse domain
to be disjoint from that acceptance box too, unless the rejecting distance
constraint already proves all children rejected. This is a distinct future
API/math/property-test change and is not included in the nine source variants.

# ShaderLOD development throughput review

The [second investigation](#second-investigation-parallelism-and-useful-work)
adds reconstructed critical paths, concrete zero-work cases, a direct End-cloud
port, reusable Iris option preparation and a measured Java allocation improvement.

October 12, 2026, Pacific time. Human-authorized investigation and improvements,
with a 60-minute elapsed budget and four GPT-6 Astra workers. The existing shader
runtime goal remains paused; this maintenance does not spend or reset its remaining
1,200-second allocation. Findings describe the sampled record, not an estimate of
total agent hours.

## Conclusion

The largest demonstrated opportunities are better delivery sequencing and reuse of
actual launcher/consumer contracts. The project already shares its shader policy,
selection/recovery service and adapter resources across ten builds. Another general
shader framework would not address the recurring problems we found.

Agents produced substantial real work, including old MakeUp/Sildur renderer gains
and newer rendering/control ports. But expensive validation and preparation often
advanced before a usable candidate, while some optimization ports targeted inactive
or very small workloads. Repeated hand-built caller assumptions then caused failures
that were unrelated to shader performance. The correction is to port a named working
mechanism through its actual selected consumer, automate repetitive authoring and
launch steps, and make the evidence required depend on the requested deliverable.

| --- | --- | --- |

The preceding BSL source investigation occupied a 71-minute observed interval without optimizer acceptance. Different scopes mean this is not a controlled productivity ratio. | Deliver the requested preview with honest limitations; do not make an unrelated certification project its prerequisite. |

More synthetic tests of the wrong assumption do not help. |

Later private operations fixed sequencing. | Maintain that final operation once; stamp only after preparation/review, then produce/freeze/preflight/launch without a model handoff. |

## Second investigation: parallelism and useful work

The follow-up asked why one worker per shader had not produced proportionate
progress over the user's roughly 72-hour experience. A fresh four-Astra team
investigated the actual dependency chain and optimization yield. Together with
the parent, it delivered two reproducible candidates and an immediately usable
developer tool. This is a second authorized
offline operation; Minecraft/GPU execution and the existing shader allocation
remain paused. The sampled records explain mechanisms of delay, not a complete
accounting of those 72 hours.

### Why source parallelism did not become delivery parallelism

In the BSL NeoForge26.2 episode, source work finished at 05:45:29 UTC. Caller
preparation was assigned at 05:56:38 and sealed at 06:06:58; launch followed at
06:07:10. Its owner had been terminal between assignments for 14m53s. The whole
source-to-runtime episode took about 35 minutes, with 21m42s between source
handback and launch. The parent was integrating/reviewing during that interval;
it is not all idle or recoverable time. But assigning preparation only after those
steps put an otherwise partly independent 10m20s task on the critical path.

In the ten-JAR preview episode, real parallel source work still left a 23m20s
integration/repair/package tail after the last initial source handback. Repeated
short repair turns and parent-mediated handoffs added dependency latency. The
shared loader, selection, producer and single client did not become independent
merely because shader files were assigned to different workers.

The operation instructions now assign consumer changes **and** authentic caller
preparation together, with late binding of the final artifact. They distinguish
exclusive frozen-input ownership from global quiet timing. Fresh untimed control
operations can permit isolated next-family preparation; existing sealed quiet
contracts remain intact. These changes target the observed queue rather than
increasing the number of unfinished shader branches.

# Development throughput: bounded transcript audit

Audit: 2026-10-13 UTC. Read-only investigation while ShaderLOD runtime work is paused. No clients, builds, benchmarks, configuration changes, or worker launches were performed. This report is the only repository file edited by this investigator.

## Finding

The strongest demonstrated bottleneck is **repeated integration of caller/observer assumptions that do not match the real consumer**, compounded by prioritizing additional proof machinery before delivering broadly usable candidates. It is not defensible to attribute all elapsed time to model compute, all checks to waste, or all failures to one cause.

A useful counterexample is in the same main session: after the human explicitly prioritized manual all-family coverage at 21:41 UTC on October 11, the team delivered ten candidate JARs at 22:31, approximately 50 minutes later. Workers made complementary selection, renderer, and shader-adapter changes; the parent integrated and tested them. That is real candidate-delivery progress, not a demonstrated all-family speedup. The preceding BSL source-identity investigation occupied a 71-minute observed interval (20:28–21:39) without establishing optimizer support. These intervals have different scopes and cannot be treated as a controlled productivity experiment, but they identify a concrete prioritization opportunity.

## Prompt, coordination and outcome claims

- **Prompt burden is measurable; causation is not.** C contains 22 repeated native-goal continuation messages totaling 171,251 characters (approximately 7,784 each), plus 188 developer-message records totaling 322,908 characters. Some are necessary runtime/hook updates; counts are persisted text, not simultaneous context, unique rules, billed tokens or attributable slowdown. Seven compactions in C support a context-management burden hypothesis, but do not prove prompt overload caused any specific defect. Keep active outcome/authorization/next step compact and avoid adding another narrative ledger.
- **Wrong worker reuse is not demonstrated by these October 10–12 samples.** B contains 48 `followup_task`, 80 `send_message`; C contains 191 and 195 respectively. Messages to running workers are valid. A historical confirmed mistake exists in `docs/USER_LESSONS.md` (“Restarting completed native workers,” including October 7), but counts alone cannot show October 11 recurrence. The explicit expiry repair above used the correct restart operation.
- **Local tests were usually not misrepresented as measured outcomes.** The inspected manual delivery and subsequent updates explicitly separate tests/builds, rendering and FPS. The problem is allocation and delivery ordering, not a demonstrated broad false-PASS habit. Do not remove those evidence distinctions.
- **“Unnecessary gates” needs specificity.** Exact resource ownership, native restoration and honest speed claims remain useful. The BSL source-identity prerequisite for manual coverage was removable because the human accepted a preview with limited evidence. It does not follow that source identity is unnecessary for a later renderer-certification claim.
- **Actual speed remained uncertain.** C's October 12 01:18 response explicitly acknowledges baseline drift and no comparable fresh gains; the current paused checkpoint likewise claims compatibility/recovery progress, not new FPS gains. This audit does not independently validate performance measurements.

## Improvements ranked for this project

1. **Use two explicit completion levels in the existing frontier:** delivered manual candidate versus certified runtime/performance result. For a requested preview, require installable output, exact scoped adapter, controls/recovery and known blockers; do not make unrelated provenance perfection a delivery prerequisite. Keep FPS/quality unverified until actually checked. The 50-minute delivery episode is the acceptance model.
2. **Make existing caller boundaries consume real producer outputs.** For any changed launcher/parser/observer, exercise one saved authentic argv, resource set, option map and receipt through the actual entry point before the dependent client. Reuse these fixtures for the small named defects; do not create a new general observer framework. Acceptance: the wrong path/default/extra-option cases above fail cheaply while the authentic record passes.
3. **Finish review before starting the finite clock.** Retain the already adopted parent-owned producer → freeze → preflight → launch operation. Worker handoffs contain prepared inputs and no live deadline; deadline creation occurs in that final operation. Acceptance: an arbitrarily delayed human/model handoff cannot expire a run that has not been armed; source/plan changes still invalidate their required checks.
4. **At an auxiliary review trigger, decide against the user deliverable.** Count preparation, repairs and reviews in one attempt. Require a concrete outcome unlocked by the next repair; if it does not block the authorized preview, ship the bounded preview and retain the diagnostic as separate unfinished evidence. A failed candidate triggers the next authorized hypothesis, not project completion.
5. **Reuse compact typed state instead of duplicating instructions.** Preserve authorization and current steering in STATUS; treat the stale immutable native-goal narrative as historical scope where it conflicts with newer steering. Add only missing enforceable operations, not longer repetitive reminders. Any claimed prompt reduction should be measured by actual injected context, not repository word count alone.
6. **Keep worker restart and acceptance evidence precise.** Use `followup_task` for a terminal worker and one acknowledgment check, as the successful sampled correction did. Independently validate consequential claims, but let a reviewer identify concrete defects rather than create an open-ended launch gate. No evidence here justifies an extra universal review layer.

These recommendations preserve real quality/restoration gates and the full 90-cell scope. They change which evidence blocks which deliverable, reduce avoidable consumer mismatches and remove model handoff latency from finite deadlines.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

Windows ownership JSON reads and atomic publication retry transient sharing errors
for at most three seconds; persistent denial still fails the operation. Normal
configuration restoration includes the five numbered FML backups for each
ShaderLOD client config. For an older interrupted report that omitted these
paths, `recover --output REPORT --preserve-generated-backups` retains newly
created known backups in that report before checking the complete original
profile map. Existing backups and unknown files retain normal ownership checks;
recovery never replays measurements.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## Records and milestone cleanup

Keep current work in STATUS, durable attempts/decisions in EXPERIMENTS, supported
procedures here and specialized routes in BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES. Extend the existing
candidate entry when adding a route; retire superseded wrappers only after checking
imports, tests and historical reproduction dependencies. Keep active experiments in
`dev/experiments`, reusable inputs/clients in `dependencies` and `run-workloads`,
and retained historical evidence in `experiment-evidence`. Do not move a pinned
active path just to satisfy this layout.

After an investigation, preserve compact raw measurements, configuration/source
identity, conclusions and any images/motion needed to support the claim. Remove
owned disposable intermediates once dependencies and restoration are checked;
there is no background cleanup requirement. For old camera sequences, put a
nonempty `.storage-retire` file beside the frames only after recording the reason
and retained evidence location. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py prune-captures`
previews exact eligible files; `--apply` uses the existing ownership/restoration
checks. Age alone is not permission to discard motion evidence. `.storage-keep`
on an ancestor protects a subtree. Unknown or still-needed evidence stays intact.

# Spatial shading LOD: minimal mod interface

2026-10-05. Spatial-adapter proposal and implemented mod surface for the
[general 50% goal](goals/general-lod-50-percent.md), coordinated with
`lod_opportunities`' lower-rate `DISTANT_DIFFUSE_IRRADIANCE` investigation. Only
the interface sources are owned by `effect_api` in an isolated worktree. The
mod surface below is implemented; storage/reconstruction is the shader owner's
separate adapter. Rendering, performance and quality require runtime acceptance.

The interface reuses immutable distance/work policy and config shape with
one additive `OPAQUE_LIGHTING` effect. Its first proposed Photon capability is opaque diffuse
irradiance reconstruction. Keep albedo, material decoding, specular/reflections,
geometry and existing shadow/AO policy controls separate. A four-to-one evaluation
rate is a plausible quality/performance tradeoff worth testing; it does not need
a formal worst-case image-error proof before a bounded experiment.

## What the budget means

The adapter's upstream unit is four diffuse irradiance evaluations for one 2×2
tile of **rendered opaque pixels**, not four display pixels regardless of TAAU.
`mediumWorkRatio`/`farWorkRatio` request a retained evaluation fraction. The pure
policy can calculate `ceil(4 * retainedRatio)`, clamped to a legal floor of one;
1/.75/.5/.25 correspond to requested counts 4/3/2/1. Do not multiply irradiance,
AO strength, shadow visibility, radiance, light intensity or albedo by this ratio.
Geometry/material edge rejection raises the legal floor to four independently
of the requested distance budget.

Use the nearest camera-relative block distance among all four valid receivers.
Full near quality means a tile cannot lower its rate when any member needs full
near shading. A conservative first experiment may retain all four through the
entire centered near transition band. Keep the documented distinction between
full-near safety and the policy's continuous distance interpolation. The policy
does not decide receiver similarity, reconstruction weights or rate legality.

The selected initial experiment supports only counts one and four. Declare that
limitation: requests for two/three select original four-evaluation fallback until
matching representative patterns/storage are implemented. Do not claim their
caps or smooth spatial transitions were consumed. The first cost control can
apply one representative only beyond the completed far band; motion/transition
inspection must then decide whether to implement intermediate rates or a stable
tile-coherent transition schedule. Such a schedule requires a declared rate
mapping; it is not automatically provided by smooth ratios or TAA. The shader
owner may instead blend full and cached irradiance in a narrow transition band,
executing both paths there; account for that extra work and do not call it K2/K3
evaluation-budget consumption.

## Implemented mod surface

`MATERIALS` is the wrong existing category: its reference adapter controls
POM/material work, while this experiment retains full-rate material and albedo
reads. `SHADOW_FILTERING`/`AMBIENT_OCCLUSION` describe protected lighting
sampling; reusing those controls would imply that their current protection or
quality budgets authorize a spatial diffuse change. `VOLUMETRICS` is unrelated.
Reuse their implementation shape, not their semantic identities.

The isolated interface source adds `OPAQUE_LIGHTING` with stable suffix
`OpaqueLighting` and config section `effects.opaque_lighting`. Reuse `mode`,
`near`, `far`, `transition`, `mediumWorkRatio` and `farWorkRatio`; no tile-size,
reconstruction-tolerance, registry or driver-specific public config is needed
for the first pinned 2×2 adapter. Adapter-owned fixed guards must be recorded
alongside source hashes. Keep defaults INHERIT, 32/96/8, unity ratios and the
existing protection setting. Experimental ADAPTIVE/far=.25 is opt-in, not a
promoted default.

Use extension **version 2** to make the new field group distinguishable from
version 1's six-effect/37-field source contract. Existing core version 2 and all
existing per-effect field names/mode numbers retain their meanings. The additive
effect adds six fields, giving 43 extension fields including the version:

| Registered source field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingMode` | 0 INHERIT, 1 FULL, 2 ADAPTIVE |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingNear` | Full-to-medium centered boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingFar` | Medium-to-far centered boundary in blocks |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingTransition` | Full centered band width |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingMediumWorkRatio` | Requested medium retained evaluation fraction |
| `shaderlodOpaqueLightingFarWorkRatio` | Requested far retained evaluation fraction |

The new consumer must require its exact accepted extension version, valid fields
and core global enable before reducing work. Absent mod/version 1/unknown mode,
unsupported pinned source, FULL or invalid conversion selects original full-rate
shading. INHERIT preserves the explicit pack-option policy. The private option
defaults OFF/full; choosing private ON can inherit its declared K4/K1 defaults.
INHERIT does not consume all custom OpaqueLighting fields. Use ADAPTIVE to prove
mod-requested bands/ratios affect the adapter. An old version-1 consumer must explicitly
review version-2 acceptance; changing the number alone cannot establish support.
No new capability uniform or automatic shader rewriting is proposed.

Do not add OPAQUE_LIGHTING to the shadow/AO budget-cut category merely because
it participates in opaque lighting. Its separate opt-in controls spatial
diffuse evaluation; existing shadow/AO protections remain true and keep their
sample budgets/radii/strengths unchanged. The adapter must independently describe
whether its reconstructed quantity includes shadow/AO modulation. Keeping their
budgets full does not by itself prove unchanged spatial shadow detail.

## Photon material and reconstruction boundary

Pinned `d4_deferred_shading.fsh:335–367` decodes per-pixel albedo, material mask,
flat normal and lightmap levels. `material.glsl` additionally carries emission,
roughness, SSS/sheen, porosity, metal flags and specular parameters; a matching
material mask alone is not a similarity certificate. Current reduced Mac options
disable normal/specular mapping, but that cannot be assumed for future profiles.

`get_diffuse_lighting` is not already a clean albedo-independent irradiance
function: SSS/sheen uses albedo, emission is added before its final albedo factor,
and the metal diffuse correction is material-dependent. Do not cache its final
RGB and divide by representative albedo. Factor only an explicitly reviewed
irradiance component, or initially restrict eligible receivers to simple opaque
nonmetal, nonemissive, non-SSS, unmapped materials. Retain the original material
emission, SSS, specular/reflection and local lighting composition where applicable.
Multiply reconstructed irradiance by each recipient's own full-resolution albedo.
Albedo texture variation itself need not reject an otherwise coherent tile: that
detail is intentionally retained at full rate.

The four-member classifier must reject sky/hand, water/translucency, overlay/
entity mismatch, invalid/out-of-bounds receivers, depth discontinuities, facing/
normal discontinuities, materially different lighting parameters and incompatible
lightmap levels. Begin with DH disabled; DH/vanilla projection boundaries select
full original until explicitly implemented. Use linear/view-space depth or a
receiver-plane test, not a raw reversed-depth delta. Guard normal/material/
lightmap variation independently; distance alone cannot authorize cross-surface
reuse. Guard thresholds are pragmatic starting values requiring quality tuning,
not an exactness requirement that forbids the experiment.

The shader owner selected **combined diffuse irradiance with representative
upstream shadow/AO**, rather than sharing only cheap sky/blocklight arithmetic.
Initially exclude SSS/sheen/emission/metals, mapped/wet materials, strong specular/
reflection paths, overlays/hand/sky and DH boundaries. Store irradiance RGB and
scalar opaque shadow in alpha; colored shadows stay outside the initial consumer.
Per-recipient albedo and eligible specular math remain full resolution, but using
the representative shadow factor in that math is still a spatial approximation.
All original shadow/AO counts, radii and strength parameters remain unchanged for
each evaluated representative; this does not mean all four original spatial
lighting evaluations occurred.

AO/bent-normal and shadow inputs can vary on a tile containing one smooth
geometric surface. Full-resolution albedo and a geometry-only classifier cannot
preserve a cast-shadow boundary by themselves. Declare this limitation and inspect
cast-shadow/foliage motion early. If it produces visible failures, a pragmatic
next guard can compare existing reconstructed AO variation and cheap center-shadow
comparisons across the four members, rejecting large spreads or ambiguous edge
values. This is a practical quality guard to tune, not a formal no-occluder proof;
its extra fetch cost must enter the kill test. Do not silently claim default
protection establishes such a fallback, or reject the entire spatial experiment
only because this guard cannot prove every worst-case pixel.

## Coherence, storage and acceptance

All members must agree on one static tile origin, rate, validity decision and
representative selection. The chosen shader plan generates a producer cache
every frame, then reconstructs eligible recipients; it does not reuse history or
randomly rotate representatives across frames. OpenGL 4.1 has
no guaranteed fragment invocation sharing; neighboring fragments cannot read a
representative's output during the same draw. A shader branch selecting one of
four fragments proves no reuse without legal inter-pass storage/synchronization.
The shader owner corrected an initial `colortex16` suggestion: pinned ordinary
Iris exposes target indices 0–15, and an external Voxy-related declaration does
not make target 16 an ordinary free cache. The revised candidate is `colortex2`
only for a strict reduced profile with NORMAL_MAPPING=false, SPECULAR_MAPPING=false
and TAAU=false, after proving its gbuffer/clipping uses are inactive. Every read,
write, render-target list, viewport and format must be audited before repurposing
it; an apparently unused sampler is not enough. A lower-rate producer viewport
must not shrink unrelated full-resolution gbuffer attachments. Verify actual
active bindings, driver limits and DH variants rather than assuming source
declarations count live units. Unsupported maps/Voxy/DH/TAAU/resource combinations
select compile-time original fallback. The current shader plan keeps colortex2's
allocation full size and uses its lower-left quarter with a half-resolution
producer viewport, rather than shrinking the gbuffer attachment. Its proposed
numbered stages are producer deferred4 and original resolve moved to deferred5;
graphics `_a` stages are not available on this pinned Iris seam. These source
constraints require driver acceptance. Conditional slot reuse is an adapter
restriction, not a general mod API assumption.
Audit Photon attachment ownership, dimensions/formats, ping-pong and clear rules;
never sample an attachment being written or reuse stale irradiance after reload,
camera/world change, resizing or mode changes. Unsupported resource state falls
back to original rendering.

The interface publishes immutable maps on config events/edits and shares one
snapshot per Iris frame notifier across program registrations. Reloads appear
at the next frame boundary without supplier allocation. Older core suppliers
remain unchanged; validate actual notifier ordering, float conversion and
reloads in the real producer/consumer pipeline. A uniform-coherent
global FULL/OFF switch must not reconstruct data generated under another mode.

Record the exact consumed fields: core global enable/version, extension version,
the new mode/bands and only the ratios/rates actually used. Uniform declarations,
NeoForge settings and package metadata remain distinct from linked driver fields,
executed reconstruction and avoided evaluations. A single ordinary explicit
consumer plus its existing measurements is preferable to another diagnostic
framework. List excluded material/dimension/DH paths as unsupported or full-rate
fallback, not partial support.

Root/shader owner should first assess whether the eligible diffuse work saves
enough to pay for tile classification, extra storage/passes and reconstruction.
Then inspect original/off/on near/far, albedo detail, contact/cast-shadow edges,
thin foliage, emissive/SSS/metal boundaries, movement and temporal disocclusion.
Iterate practical thresholds/rates to obtain little discernible quality loss;
revert or stop for flat timing or visible failures. Repeat balanced whole-frame
GPU and total-time controls after source/quality acceptance. No 75% effect-work
reduction or 50% total-throughput gain follows from the 4→1 count alone.

The isolated interface implementation passed `./gradlew test build`: all 60 tests,
including real config events/persistence, commands, coherent extension snapshots
and exact 43-field callback registration. These checks establish the requested
mod surface, not this spatial adapter's driver linking, output or speedup.

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). `baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.
