## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. G04 MakeUp `translucent_fastpath` requires `--saved-pose 9`: the maintained caller places one honey block in the backed-up save before all arms to cover the non-water/glass translucent class. Client visibility is checked; whole-save restoration removes the fixture after shutdown, including failed runs. Use `--width` and `--height` for the actual fullscreen mode (currently 2560×1600 on the local Asahi display).

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.

## Scope and actual interface

General carrier/modulator footprint weighting lives in
`shaderpacks/photon-procedural-lod/shaders/include/shaderlod/procedural_footprint.glsl`.

`shaders/program/gbuffers_all_translucent.fsh`. Three private helper files are
added. The original water source, its Belmu Gerstner comment, original Photon
LICENSE (also included in this derivative source directory), all shadow/caustic code and DH entry points remain unchanged. Relevant
entry points are world0/world-1/world1 `gbuffers_water.fsh`, through the common
translucent program, only with `PROGRAM_GBUFFERS_WATER` and `WATER_WAVES`.
Hand-water and other programs do not select the private route.

and `shaderlodEnabled == 1`. It consumes no extension1 per-effect fields, near/far

## Footprint, work avoidance and fallback

The unchanged Photon normal evaluates **three**, not five, height samples at
`coord`, `coord+(0.1,0)` and `coord+(0,0.1)`. This revision retains those finite
differences, the original normal influence, flow classification, rain/skylight
and grazing suppression. It does not use the prior analytic-gradient approximation.

Full original normal evaluation remains selected through 32 Minecraft blocks.
A smoothstep from 32 to 48 blocks enables footprint filtering. Each octave's
carrier-plus-noise upper phase-frequency bound is evaluated using the actual
raster partials of its procedural coordinate. Squared sine has a second harmonic:
weights fade between 0.125 and 0.25 fundamental cycles per raster pixel (eight to
four pixels per fundamental cycle). The first octave always stays full; full-N
amplitude normalization remains unchanged. Footprint weights are computed once
and shared by the three height evaluations.

Zero-weight octaves skip noise lookup and trigonometry **before** that work.
Each omitted octave contributes its exact uniform-phase mean, 3/8, multiplied
by its original amplitude. Low-frequency height variation remains sampled and
multiplies the entire mean-containing field. This avoids amplifying the coarse
wave through reduced-N normalization or lowering mean height merely by dropping
amplitudes. Retained coarse height/slope amplitudes are preserved.

This is not a calibrated conditional noise mean or a guarantee of equivalent
normal variance/specular energy. High-frequency slope variance is intentionally
removed; no BRDF roughness compensation is applied. The modulation bound is an
upper bound, so it can conservatively overfilter actual resolved detail. Near

## Leading candidates

### L1. Projected-footprint and temporal-confidence budgets for receiver PCF/SSS

**Algorithm/work removed.** Keep native shadow generation, native shadow distance, all casters and all lighting consumers. Reduce iterations only in expensive **receiver** kernels whose projected penumbra/material footprint and allowed temporal noise justify fewer samples. Preserve at least a real visibility estimate and the native SSS/colored shadow contribution; never substitute unshadowed lighting merely because distance is large. A small number of stable sample-count tiers avoids wildly divergent per-pixel loops. Driver: projected kernel radius, material SSS/roughness, receiver depth/normal variation, motion/history confidence, and native TAA state. This is approximate, not exact.

**Opened seams.** BSL `shadows.glsl:103–132,225–260` and consuming `forwardLighting.glsl:60–73`; AstraLex `shadows.glsl:200–208,232–258`; Sildur `deferred.fsh:565–577`. Complementary `mainLighting.glsl:264–277` is an existing instance of the policy, not a fresh saving; Photon `pcss.glsl:108–161` is already more adaptive. [GPU Gems 2 chapter 17](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems2/part-ii-shading-lighting-and-shadows/chapter-17-efficient-soft-edged-shadows-using) supplies primary precedent for coherent adaptive PCF, with explicit branch-coherence and approximation caveats. It does not predict Mac performance.

**Costs/contracts.** No new render target is intrinsically needed, so this avoids the extra full-resolution resolve of the two closed pilots. Added work is footprint calculation, tier choice and divergence; projected derivatives must be evaluated outside divergent control flow. Keep the original sampling distribution, normalization, bias, colored-depth distinctions and subsurface output definitions coherent as count changes. A source loop of twelve samples gives a local work count, not its whole-frame share. Native activation, screen coverage, fragment overdraw and compiler behavior are unknown. Large gains are unlikely for MakeUp/Solas or Complementary Medium's already tiny kernels absent another dominant path.

**Quality/compatibility.** Foliage backlighting, thin fences, colored glass and caustics can reveal noise/flicker immediately. Count changes need hysteresis or continuous stochastic transitions whose time sequence agrees with native AA. Native AA-off must use a separate conservative budget. PBR roughness/normal variation is not permission to erase visibility or SSS. DH distant terrain can rely on entirely different fallback shadows; leave that path native until its consumer is inspected. OpenGL 4.1 fragment loops suffice. Adapter burden low/medium; algorithm feasibility high, quality/performance confidence low/medium.

**Cheapest falsifier.** First inspect the actual profile's preprocessed source: if fixed expensive loops are disabled or active coverage is negligible, reject without runtime tuning. If active, parent may authorize one isolated receiver-work cost bracket that retains shadow generation and other families. A large signal earns one unchanged-scene count-tier candidate and short moving-foliage/PBR comparison. A small/no signal rejects the candidate; do not search scenes to rescue it.

### L2. Validate history before computing AO or indirect rays; sparse refresh with full fallback

**Algorithm/work removed.** On stable pixels, reuse a validated AO/bent-normal/irradiance history or launch fewer new samples; run full native work at disocclusions, changing depth/normal/material/lighting, motion, and periodic refresh. Driver: history age plus confidence/error estimates and footprint; distance only caps an error budget. Saves AO horizon searches or optional GI ray loops, not their final full-resolution consumers. Approximate: matching receiver depth/normal cannot prove unchanged off-pixel occluders or incident light.

**Opened seams/native overlap.** Photon `program/d3_ao.fsh:154–175` computes full AO **before** `:183–238` accepts history; `include/lighting/ao/gtao.glsl:39–68,103–138` bears the searches. A new early validation/sampling schedule can change work; simply increasing blending cannot. Preserve all four AO channels (AO, ambient SSS, bent normal XY) and current history depth/age. `program/d4_deferred_shading.fsh:315–333,412–450` already reconstructs those outputs. Bliss optional `ApplySSRT`, `lib/indirect_lighting_effects.glsl:372–426`, launches rays and reads previous radiance; `dimensions/composite1.fsh:1203–1205` gates activation. Bliss needs a separate indirect-history seam and is materially heavier to adapt than Photon AO. [SVGF](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/schied2017spatiotemporal/) supports variance-aware temporal reconstruction as precedent; it is not an authorization to import a whole denoiser or evidence that sparse refresh wins here.

**Inputs/invalidation/cost.** Current/previous depth, normals, material/SSS identity, motion/reprojection, projection/jitter/render-size, DH ownership and light/world changes. Reject at borders, changed resolution, pack reload, dimension changes, camera cuts, uncertain history, animated geometry and changed contributing neighborhoods. Conservative periodic refresh is necessary but not sufficient for strict equality. Photon already pays history and reconstruction reads; adding a small confidence state may reuse storage only after format/lifetime audit. New moments/normal history could consume extra targets, bandwidth and scarce samplers. Sparse fragment branches can still execute at quad/warp cost. Bliss's integrated shading cannot simply discard a pixel: unaffected outputs still need producing.

**Quality/compatibility.** Ghost AO behind moving leaves, lagged torch/GI changes and over-dark disocclusions are decisive failures. PBR normal maps and DH boundaries require separate confidence. Native TAA remains active and must not conceal stale history in still screenshots. OpenGL 4.1 ping-pong FBOs and ordinary sampling suffice; no compute/SSBO required. Adapter burden medium for Photon, high elsewhere; confidence medium algorithmically, low on net gain.

**Cheapest falsifier.** A source/control audit first establishes that actual shader-AO or optional GI is active and that stable-history decisions could bypass the expensive loop without losing other outputs. Then one parent-owned diagnostic can compare eligible stable pixel fraction against added bandwidth. Reject if eligibility collapses under representative motion or total-cost savings vanish. This is a changed premise from half-resolution AO; it must not reopen/tune the closed BSL pilot.

### L3. One current-depth hierarchy shared by long screen-space shadow/AO/indirect traces

**Algorithm/work removed.** Build conservative min/max linear-depth tiles/mips once; a ray advances over provably empty intervals and refines near overlap. Keep native sample positions/results if claiming exact skip; changing march steps, selecting averaged depth for AO, or using only a representative coarse depth is approximate. Projected ray footprint chooses hierarchy level. This targets repeated **depth fetch and position reconstruction** across effects; it does not reduce raster area by itself. [McGuire/Mara's author discussion](https://casual-effects.blogspot.com/2014/08/screen-space-ray-tracing.html) identifies min/max depth hierarchies as useful for long rays; the fetched search excerpt was available but the full blog open was blocked. [Scalable Ambient Obscurance](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2012-06_scalable-ambient-obscurance) provides primary precedent for depth preprocessing/cache-efficient AO; its algorithm is not an exact replacement of native GTAO.

**Opened seams.** Photon `include/lighting/shadows/ssrt.glsl:20–43,53–98` geometrically marches depth, already shortens far rays and exits on hit/bounds; `:128–164` deliberately chooses combined versus LOD depth. Photon GTAO `:39–68` repeatedly fetches base depth. Sildur `deferred.fsh:522–529` has sixteen contact-shadow steps. Bliss `indirect_lighting_effects.glsl:228,289,337` already uses quarter-depth; its new opportunity is conservative hierarchy traversal, not another coarse buffer. A shared producer is useful only if multiple actually active consumers amortize it.

**Resources/invalidation/cost.** Build after the relevant MC/DH depth producers and before those consumers. A hierarchy over opaque depth cannot automatically serve refraction/translucent/post-water consumers. Projection, linearization, clear values, reversed/non-reversed order, hand depth and mixed MC/DH ownership are explicit adapter fields. Rebuild every frame, or establish a much stronger producer certificate; moving scene or camera invalidates a temporal hierarchy. Raster reduction passes work on OpenGL 4.1; min/max must be generated explicitly, not ordinary averaging mipmaps. A full RG32F hierarchy through 1x1 is about `8 × W × H × 4/3` bytes (approximately 24.6 MB at 1920×1200), before extra retained buffers; more if separate MC/DH layers are needed. New passes/FBO transitions/bandwidth/branch refinement can erase all saved fetches. Existing short/contact kernels likely cannot amortize it alone.

**Quality/compatibility.** Conservative interval logic can preserve hit decisions against the represented depth and native test, but finite thickness, off-screen omissions and native SSS exit-distance semantics remain. Averages can miss thin foliage and cause light leaks. Far DH precision and normal/PBR silhouette edges require exact provenance. Burden high, confidence medium for feasibility/low for total gain. No native MDI, compute, VRS or mesh requirement; raster implementation may be slower than papers' compute variants.

**Cheapest falsifier.** Count actual bounded loop iterations/early exits in the source and identify a second active consumer **before** building a hierarchy. Reject a single short eight/sixteen-step use without a strong cost basis. If parent later authorizes a prototype, compare hierarchy build plus all consumers against originals, with one source-fixed thin-occluder case. No all-frame speed forecast follows from fewer ray steps.

### L4. Conservative uniform-shadow-footprint certificate, with native fallback

**Algorithm/work removed.** Build a min/max depth hierarchy of the current shadow map. If every texel touched by the native filter (including bilinear comparison support and bias range) is provably behind the receiver, return the exact lit result; if an opaque-only layer proves complete blockage, return the exact dark contribution where all dependent outputs permit it. Otherwise execute native PCF/blocker/SSS. Driver: projected footprint and a mathematically conservative depth bound, not distance alone. This can be exact for narrowly certified branches; a few equal test samples are only a heuristic. Filter coordinates distorted before/after offsets must be bounded in the correct space.

**Opened seams/native overlap.** BSL `shadows.glsl:103–132` and Sildur `deferred.fsh:563–577` expose full kernels without the Photon-style four-probe exit. Photon `pcss.glsl:117–161,230–240` already performs heuristic early exits, lowering residual opportunity. Complementary `SampleShadow:12–27` already avoids colored reads when possible. Thus a hierarchy must save the first probes/full remaining loops at enough receiver pixels to pay for itself; replacing already skipped work has no value.

**Inputs/outputs/cost.** Exact current depth comparison function/format, hardware PCF support, wrap/border, texel footprint, bias, colored transparent layers and blocker/SSS result liveness. Fully lit on one layer does not certify shadowcolor or SSS thickness; fully dark on shadowtex0 can be translucent, not opaque black. Keep original output for every uncertified side channel. Build only after the complete shadow transaction. Must invalidate on map clear/draw/copy/mipmap/layout, not camera/sun alone. A 2048² RG32F pyramid including base is about 44.7 MB, plus build bandwidth, new sampler and footprint bounds. ShadowColor would require further bounds/storage for generic exact certification. No ordinary shadow mipmap flag yields min/max semantics. [Iris shadow mipmap documentation](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/constants/shadow_mipmaps/) documents generation controls, not this proposed certificate.

**Feasibility/falsifier.** GL4.1 raster reduction is possible; explicit pack adapter burden medium/high and sampler feasibility unresolved with DH/PBR. Strictly conservative output should preserve native quality, but a faulty border/bias/distortion bound causes disappearing shadows. Confidence high that the bounded mathematics can be specified, low that current kernels amortize it. Cheapest falsifier is source proof that all intended certified branches still require color/SSS work or only save a few native probes; reject before allocating resources. Then an offline footprint/bound adversary, not immediate GPU benchmarking, is the next experiment.

## Additional candidates and disposition

### L5. Exact CPU shadow visibility traversal reuse — correctness track, unknown impact

Reuse shadow-only visible lists/rebuild lists/touched metadata only under identical effective inputs and producer epochs. Saves graph traversal/list assembly, **none of the GPU shadow draws**. Seam: opened `RenderSectionManager.java:139–150`; native Sodium already honors graph dirtiness generally, while exact Iris shadow behavior defeats an ordinary clean hit as described in the [source gate](../SHADOW_VISIBILITY_SOURCE_GATE_R1.md). Driver is exact equality, no visual LOD; replay ownership, task progress, frame tags, nearby-direction writes and every producer epoch are mandatory. Source foundations are unintegrated/unverified; camera and sun keys are insufficient. CPU list memory/copy/compare and frequent misses can dominate. GL-independent, potentially cross-pack, but loader/version-specific hooks are high burden; preserve shader side effects because native draws continue. Quality exactness remains conditional on the certificate; no runtime quality/performance confidence. Cheapest falsifier: complete certificate audit plus actual hit eligibility under ordinary camera movement. Existing joint shadow-family diagnostic supplies no isolated CPU share. Keep separate from GPU shadow caching.

### L6. Static/dynamic shadow-map separation — reserve research, no immediate pilot

Cache immutable solid caster depth in light-space tiles; redraw dynamic entities, waving/cutout foliage, water/caustics and newly exposed tiles, combine depths/colors correctly. Saves static caster draws/rasterization, unlike L5. Spatial/light-space tile identity and dirty geometry/material/light epochs drive updates. Exact only with unchanged projection/sample positions and complete invalidation; decimated sun/motion updates are approximate. Photon `program/shadow.vsh:89–90` voxel writes, `:103–119` animation and `shadow.fsh:106–133` time-varying water caustics are concrete counterexamples to “static blocks imply static shadow output.” Existing [cadence audit](../GENERAL_SHADOW_CADENCE_FEASIBILITY.md) identifies Iris pre-render clears, separate depth copies, matrices and shadow composites. No inspected pack exposes a ready static/dynamic transaction. Added depth/color maps, merge bandwidth, dirty-tile management and duplicate draws are high cost. GL4.1 FBO paths possible, modern GPU-driven tile lists optional; adapter burden very high. Stale foliage, moving shadows, off-view casters, DH coverage and colored PBR transparency are high risk. Cheapest falsifier: any unclassifiable side effect forces full native refresh; estimate cache eligibility before implementing. Whole-frame benefit unknown.

### L7. Multi-resolution/cascaded shadow generation retaining distant silhouettes — high-cost redesign

Allocate dense shadow texels near important receivers and coarser persistent coverage farther away, with overlapping transitions; reduce far caster raster/alpha-test work rather than deleting distant shadow cues. [Parallel-split shadow maps](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-ii-light-and-shadows/chapter-10-parallel-split-shadow-maps-programmable-gpus) is primary algorithm precedent. Photon `shadow.vsh:123–126` and `pcss.glsl:216–221`, BSL `shadows.glsl:141–180` currently implement pack-specific distorted maps/range fades, not inspected interchangeable cascades. New map arrays/atlas, per-cascade caster lists, matrix/bias/filter adaptations, transition sampling and changed shadow-side GI inputs are substantial; more cascades can **increase** geometry work. Driver projected receiver/caster footprint; approximate. GL4.1 supports conventional multipass FBO implementation; no MDI/VRS/mesh assumed. Native distortion already redistributes resolution. DH extends the receiver domain; near/far seams, thin alpha foliage and PBR/caustics are high risks. Confidence medium feasibility/low value; cheapest falsifier is draw/pass accounting showing duplicated geometry exceeds removed far raster work. Not the first reusable adapter.

### L8. Coarse diffuse irradiance with full-rate material/specular evaluation — reserve after expensive-loop proof

Evaluate smooth incident diffuse/ambient lighting on a lower-rate surface grid, reconstruct against depth/normal/material boundaries, and apply albedo/normal/PBR/specular at native rate. Removes low-frequency light evaluation without blurring texture/AA, but only where it is actually separable. Photon `diffuse_lighting.glsl:119–178` couples normals, bent normals, AO, shadows, material SSS and albedo; `:167–168` makes shadows live in bounce light. `program/d4_deferred_shading.fsh:552–582` consumes diffuse and specular lighting separately. Existing SH skylight/lightmap evaluation is already cheap relative to a ray marcher; no many-light loop was established in the inspected common paths. Extra irradiance buffer, gather reconstruction, normal discontinuity fallback and memory may exceed scalar arithmetic saved. Approximate, distance/footprint/error driver, invalidated by lighting/material/geometry change. GL4.1 feasible, high adapter burden, low gain confidence. Preserve foliage SSS, colored shadows and moving torch response; PBR normal mapping must not be applied twice or removed. Cheapest falsifier: prove the separable expression contains substantial active texture/ray work, otherwise reject. This cannot repeat the closed isolated AO/VL spatial pilots unchanged.

**Forward/deferred split matters.** Photon already exposes a deferred opaque shading seam: its full-rate G-buffer material/depth can feed a new coarse diffuse pass, followed by full-rate reconstruction and native specular at `d4_deferred_shading.fsh:577–603`. Native specular still consumes `shadows * cloud_shadows * ao` at `:582`; a full-rate sharp specular path may therefore retain shadow/AO work that was hoped to disappear. Normals are not merely a final multiply: sampling directional irradiance or retaining a small basis (rather than a single RGB diffuse result) may be necessary for normal-mapped PBR. SSS remains material/albedo/view dependent. These choices change storage and reconstruction cost substantially.

BSL `program/gbuffers_terrain.glsl:352–354` calls `GetLighting` in the terrain fragment, and `gbuffers_water.glsl:498` does so for water. Complementary terrain `program/gbuffers_terrain.glsl:329–331` calls `DoLighting` with native material, emission and subsurface fields; its water program includes the same main-lighting library at `:86`. A low-resolution diffuse pass here requires a true pipeline split: retain full-rate material/depth/silhouette production; export sufficient unlit inputs; move lighting after opaque geometry; reconstruct and combine; retain a separate transparent/water path and relevant fog/emission ordering. Merely changing the viewport of a lighting helper cannot do this. Forward transparent layers cannot all be represented by the nearest opaque G-buffer sample. This is a potentially larger work family than half-rate AO/VL, but also a larger pack redesign.

Current [Iris ColorTex documentation](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/buffers/colortex/) says resized colortex targets cannot be written by gbuffers. [Rendering directives](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/shadersproperties/rendering/) further require all render targets written by one raster program to have identical sizes. Consequently full-rate material outputs plus a resized irradiance output cannot be attached to one existing gbuffers/MRT program. Separate raster passes or a full-sized allocation with reduced viewport/subregion are options; the latter retains allocation/clear/bandwidth obligations. `scale` affects viewport, not allocation. The actual pinned-Iris `scale.deferred` key and previous successful work-area observation are in [BSL viewport correction](../BSL_VIEWPORT_CORRECTION_R6.md); current web docs do not replace that pinned behavior. Image-store exceptions are unavailable on the current native Mac baseline.

**Revised disposition:** preserve as Tier B/high-ceiling **hypothesis**, ranking above merely adding another half-rate auxiliary effect when the source/cost gate finds a substantial separable lighting family. Do not yet rank it above simpler work with proved activation. Cheapest decisive experiment is a one-pack decomposition ledger: how much expensive work moves, which full-rate consumers still force the same shadows/AO, what additional G-buffer channels/passes/samplers are necessary, and whether transparent/DH/PBR paths have a faithful fallback. A favorable ledger earns implementation planning, not immediate GPU runs.

### L9. Incremental/clipmapped voxel-light propagation — platform-qualified, absent from Mac baseline

Update only dirty voxel/light regions and their propagation neighborhoods, with coarse far cells; retains distant diffuse cues while removing repeated full-volume propagation. Photon `program/lpv/floodfill.csh:14–29,47–52` uses workgroups and writable 3D images, alternating light volumes each frame; `shadow.vsh:89–90` writes voxel data. Source native `shaders.properties:172,198,223` gates shadowcomp on COLORED_LIGHTS. Drivers dirty source/occluder epochs, camera-volume movement and light change; finite propagation and coarser grids approximate unless iterated to exact native state. Dirty frontiers expand multiple cells/iterations; changing opaque blocks can affect large regions. Needs native compute/image support, plus possibly SSBO/atomic queues in a sparse implementation, so **not native Mac GL4.1**. A raster slice fallback is a separate redesign with its own cost. High memory/adapter burden; light leaks, delayed torch changes, PBR emission and shadow-side voxel producer semantics dominate risk. Source feasibility outside Mac only; no runtime claim. Cheapest falsifier: actual active capability/native option check rejects this as a current Mac optimization before implementation.

### L10. Prefiltered moment/variance shadow representation — fast-query alternative, lower confidence for faithful quality

Replace many PCF depth comparisons with filterable moments and a visibility bound; reduce wide shadow-filter work and allow mip-selected far queries. [Summed-area variance shadow maps](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-ii-light-and-shadows/chapter-8-summed-area-variance-shadow-maps) gives the algorithm and light-bleeding/bandwidth tradeoffs. Seams: Photon `pcss.glsl:29–61,90–183`; BSL `shadows.glsl:103–132`. Changes generator representation, filter passes and every receiver; native depth needed by SSS, colored shadows, caustics and volumetric consumers cannot simply be removed. Driver filter footprint; approximate with leakage/bias changes. Extra moments and prefilter bandwidth plus retained original depth can destroy the benefit for native four/nine-tap kernels. GL4.1 fragment/FBO implementation possible, no compute required; high adapter burden, low fidelity confidence. Cheapest falsifier: a layered thin/colored occluder case with high depth variance rejects unacceptable bleeding before performance work. Not recommended for first pilot.

### L11. Receiver-contribution-certified caster pruning — distinct Tier B generation opportunity

Construct a conservative light-space demand region from **all** native receiver queries, expand for filtering/blocker/SSS footprints and relevant light rays, and omit only caster draws/regions that cannot affect that region or other shadow-pass side effects. Saves shadow generation geometry/raster/alpha work, unlike L1/L4 receiver filtering and L5 CPU traversal reuse. Driver current receiver support and caster contribution, not simply camera distance. Exact only with complete consumers and conservative bounds. The native advanced shadow frustum already restricts potentially contributing casters; savings must be beyond that baseline ([pinned source gate](../SHADOW_VISIBILITY_SOURCE_GATE_R1.md)). The opened `RenderSectionManager.java:145–150` visibility/list seam is a potential insertion point, not evidence of a valid demand mask.

Photon `pcss.glsl:29–54,117–147` shows separate blocker, distorted filter and transparent coordinates; `d4_deferred_shading.fsh:498–582` demonstrates opaque receiver use, but Photon `program/shadow.vsh:89–90` voxel writes mean zero camera shadow contribution does not prove a caster draw dead. Complementary water `program/gbuffers_water.glsl:86` consumes main lighting independently. Volumetric rays, reflection/water receivers, transparent layers, DH and off-view visible-in-reflection surfaces cannot be represented by an opaque camera-depth mask alone.

Pass order is another barrier. The [Iris program-order reference](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/programs/overview/) places shadow work before main gbuffers; a current-frame main-depth demand mask is unavailable there unless a depth/prepass or pipeline reordering is introduced. Forward lighting in BSL/Complementary consumes shadow maps during gbuffers, so simply moving shadows after their main depth creates a cycle. Previous-frame demand is approximate unless newly exposed receivers/casters/motion and all dependent effects are covered by conservative expansion and fail-closed refresh. Camera/sun equality is insufficient; producer geometry/animation, alpha/material, light, DH, render distance, projection, map layout and resource changes invalidate demand.

A CPU conservative volume or raster tile-mask path is possible on GL4.1. GPU-generated compact draw lists would add nonbaseline compute/SSBO/MDI dependencies; CPU readback can stall. Added prepass/demand generation, masks, section classification and false positives may outweigh removed draws. Adapter burden very high; correctness confidence low until the complete support certificate exists, whole-frame cost unknown. Cheapest falsifier: list every live shadow consumer and prove an available pre-shadow demand bound. If no smaller bound than native frustum survives without a new full depth pass, defer. No generation-pruning implementation or runtime experiment is recommended from this source evidence alone.

## Common contracts, portability and overlap

The reusable layer should expose **effect policy and provenance**, with bounded pinned adapters: native option/activation identity; raster/combined/DH depth semantics; receiver footprint; material/SSS flags; temporal jitter/history epoch; light/caster/resource epochs; output/channel semantics; fallback; and a resource budget. A universal insertion of distance checks or reuse from a shared `cameraPosition` is insufficient.

Current [Iris macOS documentation](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/miscellaneous/macos/) explicitly limits native macOS to OpenGL 4.1 and excludes compute, custom images and SSBOs. Conventional fragment shaders, FBO ping-pong, texture sampling and raster reduction passes form the baseline for L1–L4/L6–L8/L10. [ARB compute](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_compute_shader.txt) and [image load/store](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_shader_image_load_store.txt) are separate capability families; a compute paper is not a portable implementation. [Multi-draw indirect](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_multi_draw_indirect.txt), [NV shading-rate images](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/NV/NV_shading_rate_image.txt) and [NV mesh shaders](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/NV/NV_mesh_shader.txt) are not implied by GL4.1. None is needed for the recommended first source gates. Software sample tiers are not hardware VRS.

Mac feasibility also requires actual linked sampler demand. The [existing sampler audit](../MAC_SAMPLER_RECLAMATION_R1.md) found binding-reservation opportunities but did not establish free capacity for every DH/PBR program. New auxiliary textures, histories and min/max maps must not assume that available color attachments imply available fragment samplers. Attachment format/renderability and feedback hazards need actual pinned-Iris validation. Default and custom-image clears/lifetimes differ.

If original frame time is `T`, relevant active work is fraction `p`, and a candidate removes fraction `r` of that work but adds overhead `h*T`, idealized throughput is `1 / (1 - p*r + h)`. A 20% throughput improvement requires net time removal of about 16.7%. No measured `p`, `r` or `h` is available here; the equation is a decision threshold, not a predicted percentage. CPU/GPU overlap may make this additive model invalid, so total-frame validation still decides.

- L1 and L4 compete for the same receiver-filter samples; do not add their independent optimistic savings. L10 mostly replaces that same work.
- L2 and L3 partly overlap on AO/GI depth fetches. L3's producer cost can be shared across active effects; count it once, then measure the changed combined consumers.
- L5 saves CPU traversal while L6/L7 save GPU generation work; gains need not compound if a different bottleneck becomes dominant.
- L6/L9 share shadow-side voxel producers; skipping cached caster draws may remove required light-volume writes.
- Whole-scene raster reduction from another domain also reduces L1/L2/L3 receiver invocation counts, shrinking their remaining absolute opportunity.

The downloader writes only the exact locked artifacts under ignored
`dev/runtime/performance/`. It fails on corrupted cached files and validates
download size plus SHA256 and SHA512 before an atomic replacement. It does not
change a running client, game directory, optimizer configuration or base lock.
It refuses a target version mismatch with the base runtime lock.

Gradle selects only the named stack via `-PperformanceStack=...`; `minimal` is
the default. Runtime inputs are the lock's `stacks[stack]` members, mapped to
`dev/runtime/performance/${artifact.filename}`, never a wildcard containing all
downloaded JARs. The optional JARs belong to `localRuntime`, including the
absent-main-mod development baseline, rather than production dependencies:

```sh
./gradlew runClientLodOff -PperformanceStack=optimized -PrunDirectory=run-workloads/forest/high
./gradlew runClientLodOn -PperformanceStack=optimized -PrunDirectory=run-workloads/forest/final-adaptive
```

Use isolated profiles when switching stacks. A copied game's `mods/` directory
can contaminate a nominal minimal run, and optimizer-generated config files
persist after a mod is removed. Record the actual loaded mod list, effective
settings and configuration fingerprints in each benchmark.

## Expected budgets and compatibility inspection

ModernFix targets loading, memory, bugs, world-generation and assorted CPU
costs. FerriteCore primarily reduces memory use. Neither is a shader sampler
optimization, and a large steady-frame improvement in a warmed vanilla scene
is not assumed. Keep ModernFix's experimental dynamic resources at upstream
defaults; enabling a model-loading redesign would be a different experiment.
[ModernFix description](https://modrinth.com/mod/modernfix),
[FerriteCore description](https://modrinth.com/mod/ferrite-core).

ImmediatelyFast batches immediate rendering for entities, particles, text and
HUDs. Its benefit depends on the CPU work visible in the scene. The selected
JAR has explicit Iris compatibility: it accesses `ImmediateState` fields
present in pinned Iris and clears outline buffers at the end of Iris shadow
rendering. Its plugin enables that compatibility only when Iris is installed.
No DH-specific mixin was found in its listed configs. This narrows the static
risk but does not prove the combination renders correctly.
[ImmediatelyFast description/source](https://github.com/RaphiMC/ImmediatelyFast).

The newest README mentions `fix_slow_buffer_upload_on_apple_gpu`; that option
is absent from this 1.21.1 JAR's configuration classes. Its older
`fast_buffer_upload` option exists. Do not attribute Mac measurements to the
newer option or force an unrecognized config field.

ImmediatelyFast also touches GameRenderer and RenderType/buffer flushing.
Its inspected GameRenderer wrappers retain the original render/HUD calls;
they do not cancel ShaderLOD's outer frame-timing methods. However, added
flushes and replacement buffer sources may change the work covered by the
Iris-specific `FullyBufferedMultiBufferSource` profiling hook. Frame timing
remains the comparison metric; do not interpret a disappearing buffered-draw
scope as eliminated cost. Run low-overhead captures with `cpuLayerTiming=false`;
recheck layer scopes before using them for attribution on the optimized stack.

An [open upstream report](https://github.com/RaphiMC/ImmediatelyFast/issues/512)
describes invisible in-world Iris configuration UI on MC 1.21.1 / Iris 1.8.12 /
Sodium 0.6.13 / ImmediatelyFast 1.6.10 with many additional HUD mods. This is
not an established failure of the selected minimal optimizer stack. Check the
in-world shader settings UI; if reproduced, isolate HUD batching and record
the changed configuration. OptiFine/OptiFabric are explicitly unsupported by
ImmediatelyFast and are excluded.

EntityCulling skips hidden entities/block entities using asynchronous visibility
work. Ordinary terrain blocks, clouds, DH terrain and Photon raymarch steps
are not its target. The current forest/cloud scenes suppress mob spawning;
a gain from EntityCulling there cannot be presumed. Use a separate entity-rich
scene with visible and occluded entities. Check shadow casters and block entities
rendering beyond their block bounds. The selected JAR's listed mixins touch
entity/block-entity render dispatch; no explicit Iris/DH-specific class reference
was found in top-level bytecode. Iris behavior still needs a runtime check.
[EntityCulling description](https://modrinth.com/mod/entityculling).

## Benchmark interpretation

Use identical scenes/settings for original, patched-disabled and active packs
within each stack. Keep the mandatory Iris/Sodium versions constant and vary DH
separately. Compare ShaderLOD's incremental gain inside a stack, then report
the stack's independent gain. Keep a manual-radius and simple lower-preset
control, because smaller vanilla detail radius is an existing DH tradeoff.
Balanced run order and repeated complete JVM termination help expose thermal,
cache, background-process and first-launch variance.

The optional stack's loading and visual checks remain unverified at this
research checkpoint. No performance number or general compatibility claim is
established by artifact hashes or advertised project support.

## API contract and exact repair

OpenGL4.1 §3.8.2 (printed p.192) selects a sampler unit using ACTIVE_TEXTURE and
queries SAMPLER_BINDING with GetIntegerv; table6.15 (printed p.356) identifies that
getter. ARB_sampler_objects likewise admits the token to non-indexed Get functions
and specifies GetIntegerv for the current sampler. `glGetIntegeri` accepting an
integer argument in LWJGL does not make this token a supported indexed query on
the pinned GL4.1 context. An old returned zero cannot certify an unbound sampler.
[OpenGL4.1 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec41.core.pdf),
[ARB_sampler_objects](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_sampler_objects.txt).

All seven reads now use `GL11.glGetInteger(GL33.GL_SAMPLER_BINDING)` while the
requested unit is selected. Query exceptions propagate to existing failure paths;
no fake zero, error consumption, sampler rebinding or guard relaxation was added.

| Staged file | Context and restoration |
| --- | --- |
| `BslMipParity.java` | Both original-inspection and replay-input checks already select the input unit. Change only the getter; existing outer `finally` restores ACTIVE_TEXTURE. Both zero gates remain strict. |
| `CloudSamplerStateProbe.java` | Its sampler helper already selects the uniform's unit, with enclosing inventory restoration in `finally`. Change only the getter. Existing positive-sampler parameter observation remains intact. |
| `ComplementaryRasterActivationProbe.java` | Read sampler and physical texture in the same selected-unit scope, before restoring the saved unit. Retain the exact receipt fields and positive-sampler filter observations. |

| `ComplementaryCopyGraph.java` | Preserve the unit-range and zero-override predicates/message. Read the sampler inside the existing save/select/physical-texture scope; retain its restoration check. |
| `SpatialLayoutEvidence.java` | `NativeDriver.samplerObject(unit)` independently saves/selects/reads/restores instead of relying on caller selection. Current callers already validate the unit; interface and abstract/fake driver contracts are unchanged. |

## Capability boundary and reusable contract

The current [Iris macOS documentation](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/miscellaneous/macos/) states the native GL 4.1 boundary and missing compute/custom-image/SSBO support. On this lane use fragment/FBO passes, texture reads, explicit gradients and bounded scalar loops. Extra render targets still consume memory, attachment bandwidth and sampler slots; sixteen color buffers do not imply sixteen *free* sampler bindings. Exact linked DH/PBR demand remains unverified.

[Iris programs](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/programs/overview/) document compute pass support requiring GL 4.3; [custom images](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/buffers/custom_images/) require GL 4.2. SSBOs and compute belong to the GL 4.3 tier; image load/store predates them in 4.2. MDI requires GL 4.3 core or its extension, not a generic GL 4.1 guarantee ([Khronos MDI specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_multi_draw_indirect.txt)). None of the first four candidates needs MDI. Wave compaction, indirect dispatch and coherent image writes cannot be silently assumed in a fragment-only port. Hardware VRS and mesh shaders have additional extension/hardware requirements and are not Mac fallback algorithms; [NV shading-rate image](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/NV/NV_shading_rate_image.txt) is an explicit extension.

Proposed common data, with each pack decoding its own layout:

- **Ray contract:** origin/direction in a named space; interval; depth convention and source; footprint; original sample lattice; hit/thickness rule; native fallback.
- **Material contract:** physical/pack material class, filtered normal, roughness, height bound, atlas tile and gradients, radiometric contribution. A name such as “water” is insufficient.
- **Budget contract:** projected displacement, residual radiance or opacity bound, confidence, and native-quality fallback. Distance is one input rather than the sole trigger.
- **Resource contract:** same-frame writer/consumer, dimensions/filtering/format, live binding budget and ping-pong ownership. [Iris rendering](https://shaders.properties/current/reference/shadersproperties/rendering/) documents main/alternate composite attachments; ordinary automatic mip generation is not a conservative min/max hierarchy.
- **Temporal contract:** native jitter/history ownership; camera, projection, render size, world/dimension, material resource, weather/time/light and animation epochs. For uncertain provenance, recompute with native code. Do not infer validity from camera immobility.

These contracts transfer across loaders conceptually. Their uniform/resource delivery and exact Iris hooks must be checked independently for each loader/version artifact. This report makes no per-version support claim.

## Four strongest bounded candidates

### V1. Projected reflection traversal, first without a new hierarchy

**Removed work and driver.** B1/C1/O1/A1 repeatedly project a view-space point, fetch depth, unproject the sample, compute distances, then expand/refine the ray. A perspective-correct 2D DDA can walk screen pixels with incremental interpolation, and choose stride from projected footprint plus roughness/error rather than camera distance. It removes repeated matrix work and duplicate-pixel visits; it can also avoid holes caused by rapidly expanding 3D steps. The [McGuire–Mara paper](https://jcgt.org/published/0003/04/04/paper.pdf), §§1–3 and GLSL listing, supplies the algorithm and depth-interval treatment. Its old hardware numbers are not estimates for this project.

**Native check and exactness.** Photon P4 and Sildur S1 already step in screen space. Replacing them just because DDA is fashionable has a weaker premise. BSL/Comp/Solas/AstraLex show the stronger operation-level opportunity. New hit ordering/thickness and jitter generally change pixels: this is an approximate replacement even if it improves geometric hit accuracy. A narrower algebraic projected-increment rewrite preserving the native sample sequence could be closer to equivalent, but has not been derived or tested. Native early exits, sky fallback and material gating remain mandatory.

**Inputs and adapter burden.** Position, reflected direction, actual projection, viewport, depth, native thickness/refinement, roughness where used, and exact AA jitter phase. DH is especially consequential: B1/C1/O1 unproject DH depth with `dhProjectionInverse`, not the vanilla inverse. Either transform both depths into a proven shared space or keep separate traversal contracts; a raw min of the two nonlinear depths is invalid. Main, translucent, DH and PBR paths need separate call-site validation. A1's full DH path was not inspected. Moderate bounded adapter burden on four families, uncertain cheap transfer to the others.

**Cost and overhead.** No new target/pass/history is required for the first version; extra clipping, reciprocal interpolation, thickness tests and branch divergence remain. With long screen-space rays, one-pixel DDA may visit **more** samples than the native 30-step cap. A minimum stride/cap must preserve the declared quality bound rather than claim exactness. BSL B2 can spend another 25 radiance/alpha taps after a hit, so faster traversal cannot remove that part. Active reflective pixel coverage, average native iterations, and pass/whole-frame share are all **unknown**.

**Risks and feasibility.** GL 4.1 feasible algorithmically; no compute, VRS or mesh requirement. Water ripples, thin foliage, grazing rays, screen edges and offscreen fallback can change; PBR metals and rough materials expose hit/energy differences. Native TAA must keep its jitter/reprojection conventions. Confidence: high that integration sites exist, medium that a useful operation count reduction is available, low on whole-frame gain. Difficulty: medium.

**Cheapest decisive falsifier.** On one retained BSL or Comp water/PBR scene, first obtain native active-ray coverage and duplicate-pixel/iteration distribution under the exact loaded options. If rays rarely execute or repeated projection/traversal is a small cost fraction, reject before adapter work. A later one-version prototype must compare native/candidate hit masks and total cost with unchanged native AA, full depth fallback and original return. Do not open a scene search to manufacture reflective coverage.

### V2. Conservative cloud occupancy hierarchy with original sample positions

**Removed work and driver.** Build a conservative upper bound for cloud density/occupancy over spatial cells. Traverse empty cells cheaply and jump over original sample indices that provably lie in them. This removes density evaluations on empty primary or lighting-ray intervals. It **does not** save nested lighting at empty primary samples: P1 already avoids that work. The driver is spatial support and a bound, not distance or a global step cut. P1 is the strongest inspected starting point: detail **subtracts** from pre-detail density, and there is already a local coverage map. A max hierarchy over a valid pre-detail upper bound could certify zero-density regions; L1 has a similar erosion/coverage structure. This is a proposed extension inferred from pinned equations, not something established by the cloud-paper abstract.

**Native check and exactness.** Photon already skips Worley detail when coverage/altitude shaping is empty and already skips light rays on empty samples. The new savings therefore concern avoiding *repeated coverage/shaping probes while crossing a large empty region*, not rediscovering the existing per-sample zero test. Bliss also has existing coverage and lower-detail lighting guards. Ordinary averaged mipmaps are not upper bounds. Coarse “cheap noise then big step” heuristics can miss wisps and are approximate; they do not qualify as this candidate.

For exact native-sample equivalence, the bound must cover all texture filter support, weather/altitude shaping and floating-point rounding. Skip only sample indices whose **native** density test must return zero; keep ray origin, step, jitter and nonzero sample locations unchanged. This preserves native summation order at surviving samples. P2's radial coverage distortion means a world ray is not a straight UV segment: certification needs conservative curved-image bounds or a grid in a simpler space. Any unproved condition uses native stepping. Even with these mathematical conditions, compiled equivalence is unverified.

**Inputs/resource/invalidation.** Current coverage/shape parameters, texture contents/filter/wrap, wind/time, camera-relative map origin, shell altitude, layer identity and native sample lattice. Prefer same-frame reduction of existing coverage data, with unknown/invalid cells occupied. A static procedural-noise maximum hierarchy could avoid per-frame rebuilding but must conservatively compose animated octaves and shaping; it is not a trivial universal adapter. GL 4.1 can construct reductions through ordinary fragment/FBO passes; it cannot assume compute/image atomics. A 2D R32F hierarchy including its base costs approximately `4 × W × H × 4/3` bytes; incremental lower mips alone are `4 × W × H/3`. Extra ping-pong allocation is separate.

**Cost and overhead.** Max reductions, hierarchy fetches, coordinate bounds, cell-exit math, divergent branches and extra samplers can outweigh saved noise fetches. Native Photon checkerboarding makes the producer small already. Empty scenes may execute cheap coverage probes; dense scenes terminate early; opportunity peaks between these regimes but that is a prediction, not permission to cherry-pick. No measured cost share or speedup is available.

**Risks/feasibility.** GL 4.1 feasible in principle, high adapter burden. Wrong bounds erase thin clouds, flicker with wind and change sunlit edges. Even a correct same-frame occupancy map must respect DH terrain intersections and native cloud-history inputs; exact empty skipping should leave the latter unchanged. Reflections may use a different lower-quality cloud path. Confidence: medium on a useful conservative contract, low on net performance. Difficulty: high.

**Cheapest decisive falsifier.** Offline analysis of the pinned coverage/erosion equations and a fixed set of representative camera/weather inputs: establish conservative bound tightness and count runs of native zero-density samples. Fail if bounds are too loose, the warped map cannot be bounded cheaply, or savings are mostly work already rejected natively. Only after that source gate consider a single same-frame GPU prototype whose *full hierarchy plus consumer cost* is measured. This differs materially from the failed half-rate pilots: it preserves the producer lattice and removes empty-ray work, with no bilateral image reconstruction; new hierarchy cost is still a possible failure.

### V3. Projected POM footprint with a declared height/appearance error bound

**Removed work and driver.** P5/C3/B3/O3/A2 all contain iterative height-map traversal. Estimate the maximum projected displacement from the height range, tangent view angle, POM depth, atlas scale and UV Jacobian. If it lies below a chosen screen-space budget, use a cheaper filtered material evaluation; otherwise retain native traversal. The footprint must be anisotropic at grazing angles. A separate height hierarchy/cone-step variant can accelerate nontrivial rays rather than merely reduce samples; [GPU Gems 3 chapter 18](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-iii-rendering/chapter-18-relaxed-cone-stepping-relief-mapping) explains precomputed relaxed-cone traversal and subsequent refinement.

**Native check and exactness.** P5/B3 already distance-fade/cull POM and use explicit gradients; C3 already rejects several flat/backfacing cases. Additional opportunity is inside that native distance range for low-height or small-footprint materials. A subpixel displacement bound alone is **not** a radiance bound: a tiny UV shift across emissive/alpha/normal discontinuities can have a large visible effect. Near-zero amplitude or certified constant material tiles may permit exact suppression; general footprint LOD is approximate. Comp slope normals and POM self-shadow consume depth, so returning an unchanged UV alone is incomplete.

**Inputs/resource/invalidation.** PBR normal-alpha meaning/format, resource-pack identity, atlas tile bounds/padding, derivative/Jacobian, material flags, view/light angles, native self-shadow state, animation frame and reload epoch. Optional per-tile min/max heights and normal/appearance bounds can be generated on resource reload; animated atlases need updated bounds or native fallback. A hierarchy must not filter across adjacent atlas tiles. No frame history is needed. GL 4.1 supports the shader operations and sampled metadata; generation must use CPU or fragment reductions rather than assume compute.

**Cost/overhead and burden.** Cheap per-pixel bound is several ALU operations plus zero/one metadata fetch; hierarchy/cone maps add storage/fetches and preprocessing. Coherent material tiles may branch well; mosaic materials may not. The compiler may already fold disabled paths. Active POM fraction can be zero without a relevant PBR pack, so this cannot be a blanket pack-wide gain claim. All cost shares **unknown**. Medium adapter burden for footprint policy, high for an atlas-safe precomputed hierarchy and all side outputs.

**Risks.** PBR fidelity, emissive edges, alpha foliage, height silhouettes, self-shadow, contact depth and TAA stability; grazing movement is decisive. POM distance shrinkage merely changes quality and is not this mechanism. Confidence: high on the policy's reusability, medium on bounded source implementation, low on total gain. Difficulty: medium/high.

**Cheapest decisive falsifier.** In a fixed native-PBR material/camera set, estimate potential suppressed iterations from height range and the projected UV Jacobian while also marking discontinuous/animated materials. If almost all eligible pixels are already outside native POM range or require fallback, reject. Any later visual test must examine self-shadow and material outputs as well as color; no PBR-less speed test can validate this candidate.

### V4. Exact saturation termination in MakeUp cloud accumulation

**Removed work and proof.** M1 lines 44–82 evaluate every cloud sample. `current_opacity` starts at zero, is assigned nonnegative values in valid finite settings, and only positive contributions update `cloud_value`. `density` is set exactly once at the first positive contribution. After the loop, `cloud_value` is divided by positive `opacity_dist` and clamped to [0,1]. Once the accumulator reaches `opacity_dist`, all subsequent iterations leave final clamped opacity and first-contact density unchanged. A break at that point therefore removes subsequent cloud texture/shape evaluations without changing those mathematical outputs. This assumes native valid finite inputs and positive cloud-layer thickness/sample count; exceptional values fall back.

**Native check and integration.** No equivalent termination appears in the opened 9.5g Overworld function. The End variant was located but not fully proven; it is outside the first certificate. M2 proves a sky-only deferred caller under settings/dimension gates; M1 already returns on DH foreground. Photon/Comp/BSL/Solas/Bliss/AstraLex already have native extinction/alpha terminations, so this is a common monotone-accumulator *contract* with one confirmed missing instance, not a universal new benefit.

**Important exactness boundary.** M1 uses implicit-derivative `texture2D` inside its loop. Introducing lane-dependent termination can invalidate subsequent implicit derivatives in neighboring lanes. The native custom texture's actual filtering/mip behavior must be proven, or explicit gradients must be derived outside divergent control with equivalent LOD. A textual `break` is insufficient to claim losslessness. First-contact output, post-loop brightness shaping, final alpha, dimension/AA gates and native sample phase must remain identical. This is a certificate for possible exactness, not compiled proof.

**Cost/resources/risk.** No new pass, target, history, sampler or reconstruction; one comparison per iteration. Mixed empty/dense lanes may keep hardware groups running, limiting savings. Saturation frequency, native sample count and total cost share are **unknown**; sky-only/DH gates narrow coverage. Still/motion risks should be small if the derivative contract is solved, but there is no actual quality evidence. GL 4.1 feasible. Confidence: high on scalar accumulator proof, medium pending derivatives, low on whole-frame gain. Difficulty: low/medium.

**Cheapest decisive falsifier.** First establish effective `gaux2` filter/mipmap state and source-level derivative equivalence, then count where the native accumulator saturates before its last iteration for fixed representative rays. Reject if rare or incoherent. If it survives, the orchestrator could later authorize one exact-adapter work/source/On–Off quality and total-cost screen. A null result closes it; it does not justify denser clouds or a new preset. It is deliberately a low-cost probe, not the main justification for a 20% goal.

## Whole-frame cost, overlap and historical counterexamples

Let `f` be the fraction of **baseline total frame time on the limiting path** removable by a mechanism, `r` the removed fraction of that work and `h` its added cost normalized to the same baseline. In a simplified serial GPU model, speedup is `1 / (1 - f*r + h)`. A 20% throughput increase needs `f*r - h >= 1/6`. For illustration only, if `f = 0.30` and `h = 0.02`, the mechanism must remove at least 62.2% of that family's work. These inputs are not measured here. If CPU and GPU overlap, reducing a nonlimiting GPU pass may change total frame time negligibly; summing CPU and GPU pass costs is wrong.

- V1 and V5 mainly attack the same reflection traversal. V8 reduces rays that V1/V5 would trace; assess marginal savings after the first method, not three baseline percentages. B2 radiance reconstruction survives V1 and may dominate afterward.
- V2 removes primary empty cloud probes. V6 removes light probes at occupied samples. They can partly compound, but native zero-density/opacity guards and V10 termination reduce both opportunities. Photon P3 already reduces the invocation count that any cloud proposal can accelerate.
- V7 fog sharing overlaps lighting/shadow-receiver savings in another research track. A shared depth hierarchy or normal metadata may amortize cost across mechanisms, but only count one verified producer and all consumers/allocations; no free-infrastructure assumption.
- V3 applies only to POM-enabled resource/material coverage; V9 only to water consumers. They can coexist, yet independent disjoint-pixel opportunities do not automatically sum to a large whole-frame fraction.
- A GL 4.1 fragment shader still launches inactive screen pixels unless draw/viewport coverage is actually reduced. Branch masks may save texture/ALU work but are not hardware VRS. Savings depend on coherent lane behavior and compiler output, not scalar loop counts alone.

The closed Complementary half-VL and BSL half-AO pilots proved work-area changes without useful total-frame gain. Do not reopen them unchanged or rebrand their resolver as a new generic LOD. V2 and V4 avoid a new full-resolution reconstruction pass; V1 first avoids a new target entirely. V5/V6/V7/V8 introduce significant new work and must explicitly earn that cost. Photon TAAU's human ~10% Mac/~15% Windows and qualified old coast 8.84–9.20% are historical observations, not portable forecasts. The 2→−1→2 shadow-family sequence changes several dependent effects and does not supply isolated fog/cloud/SSR cost shares.

**Strategic shortlist:** V1 for the four inspected view-space SSR families; V2 for Photon/Bliss after a conservative-bound source gate; V3 when PBR materials make its cost live. **Cheapest exactness/cost probe:** V4, with modest expectations because sky coverage and native cloud complexity constrain its ceiling.

If the certificate fails or saturation is sparse, close V4 without a runtime rescue. If the orchestrator instead needs a candidate with a larger plausible ceiling first, choose V1's active-work distribution gate on an existing retained BSL/Comp scene; do not implement a hierarchy before proving that rays are a material cost. ### Ranking change and investment disagreement

My initial R1 put occupancy second because of its reusable exact-zero contract. The retained density result plus native checkerboard/coverage evidence downgrades it below C5/C6 and C7 **unless** a coarse-empty-run gate proves a substantially different removed-work set. This is an evidence-based priority change, not rejection of all spatial hierarchies.

The first experiment and largest investment need not be the same. C8 is more certain to execute over all pixels than C2/C5 optional loops and has a narrow exactness target; it therefore survives as a short certificate/cost test. Its low plausible ceiling means it should not displace the higher-impact source gates for C1 or active C5/C2/C6. If C8 needs a large resource rewrite or new observation framework, its cheap-test advantage disappears and I would choose the existing projected-POM activation/acceptance gate instead. The latter already has a private candidate and qualified visible material activation in a retained report, although no accepted speed/quality result.

There is no justification for discarding every high-ceiling hypothesis because cost shares are unknown, nor for building infrastructure before obtaining a denominator. I recommend two separate ranking columns in the synthesis: **probability/cost of a decisive next test** and **conditional capacity to affect a large frame fraction**. Label C8/V4 as small, cheap exact probes; C1/C5/C2/C6 as potentially broader but conditional; C3/C4/C7/C9/C10/C11 as explicit source/cost gates with higher uncertainty. C12 remains a preexisting correctness track.

### Overlap graph in words

C1 scales invocations for C2–C7/C9 and part of C8, while its reconstruction is additional fixed/full-rate work. C10 removes shaded surfaces on which C5/C6/C9 would run. C2/C3 improve the same ray traversal; C7 bypasses rays C3 would accelerate. C6/C11 remove the same receiver taps. C4 and cloud-light fields affect different primary-empty/occupied-light work but native termination limits both. C8 removes a separate copy's traffic, yet lowering its working resolution under C1 lowers its remaining payoff. C12 targets CPU traversal, whose gain may appear only after sufficient GPU work has been removed. The combination must be assessed incrementally against the same faithful original denominator, never by summing optimistic local percentages.

# ShaderLOD-next: agent-first porting plan

Status: implementation of packages A–D and lightweight agent development exercises authorized by Philip on 10 November 2026. Benchmark redesign (E), optimization research/workflow proof (F), and high-level skills/shared agent operations (G) remain deferred. Live work requires a currently available compatible machine; an unavailable allocation is a partial state, never a synthetic substitute. Current implementation and verification status is maintained below.

## 1. Outcome and settled constraints

The goal is a short, reliable development loop: inspect measured expensive work, state a plausible mechanism, implement one optimization through a supported extension, verify activation and correctness, measure through the maintained harness, iterate, then close with scoped evidence. More checks, instructions, or generated code are not success by themselves.

Philip's latest decisions govern this plan:

- Preserve `/home/philip/ShaderLOD` and the lowercase historical checkout. Leave historical evidence there. Refactor selected behavior into next; do not transplant its candidate graph or clean up the old repositories.
- Next may be substantially rebuilt, but remains local-only with no remote/push. Keep small reversible commits and preserve unrelated edits.
- Start with Complementary Reimagined and DH on a compatible first machine. Add shaders and hardware gradually. DH absence must still be safe; enabled-DH behavior is part of the first intended product.
- Include native shader selection, config, Apply/Off/Cancel/recovery, and the basic machinery for developing and loading NEW optimizations. All old candidates remain parked. Do not port auto-tuning, unrelated loader/version targets, or old campaign launchers.
- Preserve original archives, effective native settings, resolution and AA. Unsupported combinations must remain explicit; do not silently lower settings to obtain a pass.
- Ban comments/docstrings in owned code. Refactor unclear code into understandable types, names, and responsibilities. Do not merely move excuse-laden comments into decisions. Preserve required attribution through narrow exceptions; shader directives are executable syntax, not comments.
- Root-only instructions; `CLAUDE.md` references `AGENTS.md`. No arbitrary instruction byte cap. One findings index if it remains useful, with accepted results showcased in README and other findings separately accessible.
- Agents work autonomously within the authorized task. Routine tests, check repairs, bounded recovery, and safe resource reclamation do not require repeated approval. New goals, destructive operations, unsupported scope changes, and weakened acceptance semantics do.
- No hosted CI/PR/review bureaucracy is required. Local verification must stand on its own. Actual benchmark methodology remains a later design task; this plan specifies interfaces and integrity requirements only.

The hierarchy for every recurring problem is: eliminate the bad state through architecture; encode the invariant in types/API behavior; verify it with tests/static checks; use a tool or skill for operational procedure; use instructions for the remaining judgment. A new rule must explain the failure it prevents and the legitimate path it leaves available.

## 3. What to add, remove, and adapt

### Add

1. A typed optimization module contract, generated registration, activation witnesses, and add/remove extension tests.
2. Explicit owners for configuration transactions, runtime lifecycle, artifact publication, and disposable workspaces; recovery is part of their APIs.
3. One versioned wire contract with Java/Python conformance fixtures and closed decoding at boundaries.
4. A fast CPU feedback lane and a complete closure lane; trustworthy incremental reuse and actionable diagnostics.
5. A bounded runtime execution interface shared by verification, profiling, and later benchmarks; structured status, cancellation, recovery, and resource accounting.
6. Managed storage classification and safe reclamation before resource failure becomes a blocker.
7. One current plan, one findings index, immutable evidence references, and generated/validated accepted-result presentation.
8. An explicit optimization workflow tying candidate selection to observed cost and scope; end-to-end rehearsal before claiming agent readiness.

### Remove

1. Text/filename bans that infer raw output, plans, GPU allocation, or architectural ownership from common words.
2. The hard instruction-size cap, seven-finding limit, and exact global test-name list.
3. Mandatory hosted CI/CODEOWNERS artifacts and personal review of every test/check edit as completion requirements.
4. Stage-number literals in runtime refusal logic; missing capabilities should be reported by capability, not migration numbering.
5. Unused discovery outputs, misleading report counts, and checks with no subjects masquerading as production coverage.
6. Stale MakeUp-first/four-shader-first instructions and per-piece approval stops.
7. Rejected candidate source, hooks, registrations, and fixtures that no longer protect shared behavior from the active tree after closure and preservation.

### Adapt

1. Keep a comment ban, but distinguish comments from shader preprocessor syntax, licenses, string data, and digest-pinned third-party inputs.
2. Keep one owner per durable value; do not turn the result publisher into the only package allowed to perform any I/O.
3. Keep required-test/no-skip guarantees; make suite obligations and behavior IDs stable while normal test discovery grows.
4. Keep self-tests, but rerun expensive tool specimens when their inputs change and at explicit clean verification, not blindly on every edit.
5. Keep pack isolation; generate a deterministic typed provider index consumed by the actual application and CLI.
6. Keep one findings index, not one ever-growing narrative file or multiple manually maintained verdict tables.
7. Keep no GPU scheduling/lease service. Replace the racy “check processes, then launch” contract with demonstrable single-owner execution; see the explicit policy tradeoff in section 8.
8. Keep source parity and CPU-before-live gates, but make them executable progress gates within authorized work rather than requests for Philip's attention.
